title.zh: 卷二十一 志第十一 樂三
title.raw: 卷二十一 志第十一 樂三 Volume 21 Treatises 11: Music 3

translations.literal: Treatise 11: Music 3
translations.idiomatic: Treatise 11: Music III

translations.literal: The four pieces of "Dan Ge" (Plain Song) come from the Han era.
translations.idiomatic: The four Plain Song pieces date from the Han dynasty.

sentences.zh: 無弦節，作伎，最先一人倡，三人和。

translations.literal: Without string rhythm; in performance, first one person leads the singing, three harmonize.
translations.idiomatic: They use no string accompaniment for the beat; in performance one singer leads and three others join in harmony.

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Wei was especially fond of them.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Wei was especially fond of these pieces.

sentences.zh: 時有宋容華者，清澈好聲，善唱此曲，當時特妙。

translations.literal: At the time there was Song Ronghua, whose voice was clear and fine, skilled at singing this tune—then exceptionally marvelous.
translations.idiomatic: There was a singer named Song Ronghua whose voice was clear and beautiful; he excelled at these songs and was celebrated in his day.

translations.literal: From the Jin onward it was no longer transmitted, and thus perished.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Jin dynasty the tradition has not been handed down, and the pieces are lost.

translations.literal: "Xianghe" (Harmony) is an old Han song.
translations.idiomatic: The Harmony songs are an old Han repertoire.

translations.literal: Silk and bamboo alternate in harmony; the one who holds the beat sings.
translations.idiomatic: String and wind instruments answer one another in harmony while the beat-keeper sings.

sentences.zh: 本一部，魏明帝分為二，更遞夜宿。

translations.literal: Originally one ensemble; Emperor Ming of Wei divided it into two, alternating night and day.
translations.idiomatic: Originally there was a single ensemble; Emperor Ming of Wei split it into two groups that performed in alternation day and night.

sentences.zh: 本十七曲，朱生、宋識、列和等復合之為十三曲。

translations.literal: Originally seventeen tunes; Zhu Sheng, Song Shi, Lie He, and others recombined them into thirteen tunes.
translations.idiomatic: There were originally seventeen pieces; Zhu Sheng, Song Shi, Lie He, and others reworked them into thirteen.

translations.literal: "Xianghe" (Harmony)
translations.idiomatic: Harmony Songs

translations.literal: "Driving Six Dragons" / "Air Rising Song" — lyrics by Emperor Wu
translations.idiomatic: "Driving Six Dragons" (tune: "Air Rising Song") — text by Emperor Wu of Wei

sentences.zh: 駕六龍乘風而行，行四海外。

translations.literal: Driving six dragons, riding the wind to go, traveling the four seas beyond.
translations.idiomatic: I drive six dragons and ride the wind, journeying to the far reaches of the four seas.

sentences.zh: 路下之八邦，曆登高山，臨溪穀，乘雲而行，行四海外，東到泰山。

translations.literal: The eight domains along the road; passing climbing high mountains, overlooking streams and valleys, riding clouds to go, traveling the four seas beyond, east to Mount Tai.
translations.idiomatic: Through the eight lands along the way I climb lofty peaks and look down on streams and ravines; riding the clouds I travel beyond the four seas, eastward to Mount Tai.

sentences.zh: 仙人玉女，下來翱游，驂駕六龍，飲玉漿，河水盡，不東流。

translations.literal: Immortal maidens descend to soar and roam; paired with six dragons, drinking jade nectar—the river's waters exhausted, not flowing east.
translations.idiomatic: Immortal maidens descend to soar with me; with six dragons as my team I drink jade nectar, and the river runs dry and ceases to flow eastward.

translations.literal: Relieving the sorrowful belly, drinking jade nectar.
translations.idiomatic: To ease a troubled heart, I drink jade nectar.

translations.literal: Upholding and proceeding, east to Mount Penglai.
translations.idiomatic: I press on in reverence, east to Mount Penglai.

translations.literal: Ascending to Heaven's Gate.
translations.idiomatic: I ascend to the Gate of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 玉闕下，引見得入，赤松相對，四面顧望，視正焜煌。

translations.literal: Beneath the jade tower-gate, led in to be received; facing Red Pine, looking about on all sides—the vision just blazing bright.
translations.idiomatic: Below the jade gate I am led in to audience; I face Red Pine and look about on every side—the sight is dazzling and bright.

sentences.zh: 開王心正興，其氣百道至，傳告無窮。

translations.literal: Opening the king's mind, just flourishing; its qi arrives in a hundred paths, announcements without end.
translations.idiomatic: The king's mind opens and flourishes; his vital force arrives along a hundred paths, and proclamations are endless.

sentences.zh: 閉其口，但當愛氣，壽萬年。

translations.literal: Close the mouth; only ought to cherish qi—life ten thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: Keep silent and cherish your breath alone, and you may live ten thousand years.

translations.literal: East to the sea, joining with Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Eastward to the sea, where earth meets sky.

translations.literal: The way of immortals: emerging from the hidden, entering the dark.
translations.idiomatic: The path of immortals passes from the hidden depths into the dark unknown.

sentences.zh: 常當專之，心恬憺無所愒欲，閉門坐自守，天與期氣。

translations.literal: Constantly ought to concentrate on it; the mind tranquil and free of all greedy desire—shut the door, sit and guard oneself; Heaven grants the appointed qi.
translations.idiomatic: You must devote yourself to it always: keep the mind calm and free of craving, shut your door and sit in self-restraint, and Heaven will grant you the breath of the appointed time.

sentences.zh: 願得神之人，乘駕雲車，驂駕白鹿，上到天之門，來賜神之藥。

translations.literal: I wish to obtain a divine person, riding a cloud carriage, paired with white deer, ascending to Heaven's Gate, coming to bestow divine medicine.
translations.idiomatic: May I meet a divine being who rides a cloud chariot with white deer in harness, ascends to the Gate of Heaven, and bestows the elixir of immortality.

translations.literal: Kneeling to receive it, revering the spirit in fasting.
translations.idiomatic: I kneel to receive it and fast in reverence to the divine.

translations.literal: Ought to be thus; the Way comes of itself.
translations.idiomatic: Do this, and the Way will come to you of its own accord.

sentences.zh: 華陰山，自以為大，高百丈，浮雲為之蓋。

translations.literal: Mount Huayin, deeming itself great—a hundred zhang high; floating clouds are its canopy.
translations.idiomatic: Mount Huayin thinks itself mighty, rising a hundred zhang; floating clouds form its canopy.

sentences.zh: 仙人欲來，出隨風，削之雨。

translations.literal: Immortals wishing to come emerge following the wind, trimmed by rain.
translations.idiomatic: When immortals wish to come, they emerge on the wind and are swept by the rain.

sentences.zh: 吹我洞簫鼓瑟琴，何誾誾，酒與歌戲。

translations.literal: Blowing my hollow flute, striking zithers and lutes—how genial; wine and song in play.
translations.idiomatic: They play my panpipes and zithers—how gracious the gathering, with wine and song for sport.

sentences.zh: 今日相樂誠為樂，玉女起，起儛移數時。

translations.literal: Today mutual joy is truly joy; jade maidens rise, rise dancing for several moments.
translations.idiomatic: Today's shared delight is true delight; the jade maidens rise and dance for a time.

sentences.zh: 鼓吹一何嘈嘈，從西北來時，仙道多駕煙，乘雲駕龍，鬱何蓩蓩。

translations.literal: The wind-and-drum how noisy; coming from the northwest, the immortal way mostly rides mist, riding clouds and driving dragons—how lush and dense.
translations.idiomatic: How loud the drums and pipes! Coming from the northwest, the immortals ride mostly on mist, mounting clouds and driving dragons in dense profusion.

sentences.zh: 遨游八極，乃到崐崘之山，西王母側。

translations.literal: Roaming the eight extremities, then arriving at Mount Kunlun, beside Queen Mother of the West.
translations.idiomatic: Roaming the eight directions, I come to Mount Kunlun at the side of the Queen Mother of the West.

sentences.zh: 神仙金止玉亭，來者為誰？

translations.literal: Immortals—gold stops, jade pavilions; who comes?
translations.idiomatic: At the immortals' golden halt and jade pavilion—who is arriving?

translations.literal: Red Pine and Wang Qiao—the gate of virtue's turning.
translations.idiomatic: Red Pine and Wang Qiao—the gateway of revolving virtue.

sentences.zh: 樂共飲食到黃昏，多駕合坐，萬歲長宜子孫。

translations.literal: Joyfully eating and drinking together until dusk; many carriages joined in sitting—ten thousand years, long fitting for descendants.
translations.idiomatic: We feast and drink together until dusk, many chariots drawn up side by side—may you live ten thousand years, long blessed with descendants.

sentences.zh: 游君山，甚為真，磪{石嵬}砟硌，爾自為神。

translations.literal: Roaming Mount Jun, very true; rugged and craggy—you yourself are divine.
translations.idiomatic: Roaming Mount Jun, how real it is—crags towering and steep; you yourself are a spirit.

sentences.zh: 乃到王母臺，金階玉為堂，芝草生殿傍。

translations.literal: Then arriving at the Queen Mother's terrace—golden steps, jade for the hall; spirit grass grows beside the palace.
translations.idiomatic: I come to the Queen Mother's terrace with golden steps and a hall of jade; spirit grass grows beside the palace.

translations.literal: East and west wings; guests fill the hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the east and west wings, guests fill the hall.

sentences.zh: 主人當行觴，坐者長壽遽何央。

translations.literal: The host ought to pass the cup; those seated—long life, how not at center.
translations.idiomatic: The host should pass the wine; may those seated enjoy long life without end.

sentences.zh: 長樂甫始宜孫子，常願主人增年，與天相守。

translations.literal: Everlasting joy just beginning fits for grandsons; constantly wishing the host increase years, guarding with Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Everlasting joy has just begun—blessings on your descendants; may the host ever add years and keep company with Heaven.

translations.literal: "At the First Birth" / "Essence Array" — lyrics by Emperor Wu
translations.idiomatic: "At the First Birth" (tune: "Essence Array") — text by Emperor Wu of Wei

sentences.zh: 厥初生，造化之陶物，莫不有終期。

translations.literal: At the first birth, the potter of creation's fashioned things—none lack a final term.
translations.idiomatic: From the first beginning, all things shaped by creation's hand must reach an end.

sentences.zh: 莫不有終期，聖賢不能免，何為懷此憂。

translations.literal: None lack a final term; sages and worthies cannot escape—why harbor this worry?
translations.idiomatic: Nothing is exempt, not even sages—so why carry this grief?

sentences.zh: 願螭龍之駕，思想崐崘居。

translations.literal: I wish for hornless-dragon carriage, thoughts fixed on dwelling at Kunlun.
translations.idiomatic: Would that I might ride hornless dragons and dwell in thought upon Mount Kunlun.

sentences.zh: 思想崐崘居，見期於迂怪，志意在蓬萊。

translations.literal: Thoughts fixed on dwelling at Kunlun—meeting appointed in remote marvel; intent set on Penglai.
translations.idiomatic: My mind dwells on Kunlun, my tryst with the marvelous and remote, my heart set on Penglai.

sentences.zh: 志意在蓬萊，周孔聖徂落，會稽以墳丘。

translations.literal: Intent set on Penglai; Zhou's Kong the Sage passed away, Kuaiji marked by tomb mounds.
translations.idiomatic: My heart is on Penglai—yet Confucius the sage has gone, and Kuaiji holds his grave mounds.

sentences.zh: 會稽以墳丘，陶陶誰能度，君子以弗憂。

translations.literal: Kuaiji marked by tomb mounds—carefree, who can cross? The noble person thereby does not worry.
translations.idiomatic: Kuaiji holds those tombs—who can cross the boundless joy? The noble person does not grieve.

sentences.zh: 年之暮奈何，過時時來微。

translations.literal: The year's dusk—what to do? Passing time, time comes slight.
translations.idiomatic: What can be done when the year grows old? Time passes, and each moment grows faint.

translations.literal: "South of the Yangzi, Lotus May Be Picked" / "South of the Yangzi" — old lyrics
translations.idiomatic: "South of the Yangzi, Lotus May Be Picked" (tune: "South of the Yangzi") — traditional text

sentences.zh: 江南可採蓮，蓮葉何田田。

translations.literal: South of the Yangzi, lotus may be picked—how lush the lotus leaves.
translations.idiomatic: South of the Yangzi the lotus may be gathered—how thick the lotus leaves grow.

sentences.zh: 魚戲蓮葉間，魚戲蓮葉東，魚戲蓮葉西，魚戲蓮葉南，魚戲蓮葉北。

translations.literal: Fish play among lotus leaves; fish play east of lotus leaves, west of lotus leaves, south of lotus leaves, north of lotus leaves.
translations.idiomatic: Fish sport among the lotus leaves—fish sport east of the leaves, west of the leaves, south of the leaves, north of the leaves.

translations.literal: "Between Heaven and Earth" / "Crossing the Passes and Mountains" — lyrics by Emperor Wu
translations.idiomatic: "Between Heaven and Earth" (tune: "Crossing the Passes and Mountains") — text by Emperor Wu of Wei

translations.literal: Between Heaven and Earth, the human is honored.
translations.idiomatic: Between Heaven and Earth, nothing is nobler than humanity.

translations.literal: Establishing a lord to shepherd the people, making for them standards and rules.
translations.idiomatic: A ruler is set over the people to govern them and give them law.

translations.literal: Cart ruts and horse tracks weave warp and woof through the four extremities.
translations.idiomatic: Cart tracks and hoofprints span the four corners of the realm.

translations.literal: Ascending and descending through dark and light, the common folk multiply and thrive.
translations.idiomatic: Rulers rise and fall through fortune and misfortune, and the people multiply and flourish.

sentences.zh: 於鑠賢聖，總統邦域，封建五爵，井田刑獄。

translations.literal: How brilliant the sages and worthies, presiding over the realm; enfeoffing the five ranks, well-field penal codes.
translations.idiomatic: How glorious the sages who ruled the realm, enfeoffed the five ranks of nobility, and established well-field allotments and penal law.

translations.literal: There were burned red-letter records; no universal pardon and redemption.
translations.idiomatic: Criminals were marked with burned records, and there was no blanket amnesty.

translations.literal: Gao Yao's "Initial Punishments"—how could there be dereliction of duty?
translations.idiomatic: Under Gao Yao's "Initial Punishments," how could officials neglect their duties?

translations.literal: Alas for later ages—changing institutions, altering laws.
translations.idiomatic: Alas for later ages that changed institutions and altered the laws.

translations.literal: Toiling the people for the lord, conscripting and levying their strength.
translations.idiomatic: The people were worn out for their rulers, conscripted and taxed for their labor.

translations.literal: Shun lacquered his food vessels—ten states rebelled;
translations.idiomatic: When Shun lacquered his bowls, ten states rose in revolt;

translations.literal: not matching Tang Yao, whose rafters were unplaned.
translations.idiomatic: yet he could not match Tang Yao, who left his rafters unplaned.

translations.literal: The age sighs for Bo Yi, wishing thereby to sharpen custom.
translations.idiomatic: The age sighs for Bo Yi, hoping to reform the manners of the people.

translations.literal: Extravagance is the greatest evil; frugality is the respectful virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Extravagance is the greatest vice; frugality is the virtue of reverence.

translations.literal: Xu You declined and yielded—how could there be lawsuits and disputes?
translations.idiomatic: When Xu You yielded his place, how could there be lawsuits and quarrels?

translations.literal: Universal love and exalting unity—the distant become kin.
translations.idiomatic: With universal love and exalting unity, even strangers become kin.

translations.literal: "Eastern Light!" / "Eastern Light!" — old lyrics
translations.idiomatic: "Eastern Light!" (tune: "Eastern Light!") — traditional text

translations.literal: Eastern light!
translations.idiomatic: Eastern light!

translations.literal: Cangwu—why not!
translations.idiomatic: Cangwu—why not there too!

sentences.zh: 倉梧多腐粟，無益諸軍糧。

translations.literal: Cangwu has much rotted grain—no benefit to the armies' provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Cangwu holds rotting grain in plenty, useless for the armies' rations.

sentences.zh: 諸軍游蕩子，蚤行多悲傷。

translations.literal: The armies' roaming wastrels—early marching, much grief and sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: The armies' idle wanderers march at dawn, heavy with grief.

sentences.zh: 《登山有遠望》 《十五》 文帝詞

translations.literal: "Climbing a Mountain, Gazing Afar" / "Fifteen" — lyrics by Emperor Wen
translations.idiomatic: "Climbing a Mountain, Gazing Afar" (tune: "Fifteen") — text by Emperor Wen of Wei

sentences.zh: 登山而遠望，谿谷多所有。

translations.literal: Climbing a mountain and gazing afar—streams and valleys have much in them.
translations.idiomatic: I climb the mountain and gaze far off; streams and valleys hold riches in plenty.

sentences.zh: 楩柟千餘尺，眾草之盛茂。

translations.literal: Nanmu trees over a thousand chi; the mass of grasses flourishing lush.
translations.idiomatic: Nanmu trees rise more than a thousand feet; grasses flourish in abundance.

translations.literal: Flowers and leaves dazzle men's eyes.
translations.idiomatic: Blossoms and leaves dazzle the eye.

translations.literal: Five colors—hard to record them all.
translations.idiomatic: Their five colors are beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 雉雊山雞鳴，虎嘯谷風起。

translations.literal: Pheasants call, mountain cocks cry; tigers roar, valley winds rise.
translations.idiomatic: Pheasants call and mountain cocks crow; tigers roar and valley winds rise.

sentences.zh: 號羆當我道，狂顧動牙齒。

translations.literal: A roaring bear blocks my path, wildly turning its head, moving its teeth.
translations.idiomatic: A roaring bear blocks my path, turning its head and baring its teeth.

sentences.zh: 《惟漢二十世》 《薤露》 武帝詞

translations.literal: "Only Han's Twenty Generations" / "Dew on the Leeks" — lyrics by Emperor Wu
translations.idiomatic: "Only Han's Twenty Generations" (tune: "Dew on the Leeks") — text by Emperor Wu of Wei

sentences.zh: 惟漢二十世，所任誠不良。

translations.literal: Only Han's twenty generations—the entrusted were truly not good.
translations.idiomatic: Han had endured twenty generations, yet those entrusted with power were truly unworthy.

sentences.zh: 沐猴而冠帶，智小而謀強。

translations.literal: A macaque bathed and capped—small wisdom yet plotting strength.
translations.idiomatic: A monkey in cap and sash—small wits but grand ambitions.

sentences.zh: 猶豫不敢斷，因狩執君王。

translations.literal: Hesitating, not daring to decide—using the hunt to seize the king-lord.
translations.idiomatic: Hesitating and afraid to act, they seized the emperor during a hunt.

sentences.zh: 白虹為貫日，己亦先受殃。

translations.literal: A white rainbow pierced the sun—he himself first received calamity.
translations.idiomatic: A white rainbow pierced the sun, yet he was the first to suffer ruin.

sentences.zh: 賊臣持國柄，殺主滅宇京。

translations.literal: The traitor minister held the state's handle, killed the lord, extinguished the capital.
translations.idiomatic: A traitorous minister seized the reins of state, murdered his sovereign, and destroyed the capital.

sentences.zh: 蕩覆帝基業，宗廟以燔喪。

translations.literal: Overturning and destroying the imperial foundation; ancestral temples thereby burned and lost.
translations.idiomatic: He overturned the imperial foundation and burned the ancestral temples to ruin.

sentences.zh: 播越西遷移，號泣而且行。

translations.literal: Scattered westward in migration, wailing and yet marching.
translations.idiomatic: The court was driven west in exile, weeping as it went.

sentences.zh: 瞻彼洛城郭，微子為哀傷。

translations.literal: Gazing on those walls of Luo city—Weizi made mourning and grief.
translations.idiomatic: Gazing on the walls of Luoyang, Weizi was moved to grief.

sentences.zh: 《關東有義士》 《蒿里行》 武帝詞

translations.literal: "East of the Pass, Righteous Men" / "Procession Through the Wilds" — lyrics by Emperor Wu
translations.idiomatic: "East of the Pass, Righteous Men" (tune: "Procession Through the Wilds") — text by Emperor Wu of Wei

sentences.zh: 關東有義士，興兵討群凶。

translations.literal: East of the Pass there were righteous men, raising troops to punish the mass of villains.
translations.idiomatic: East of the Pass righteous men rose and took arms against the rebels.

sentences.zh: 初期會孟津，乃心在咸陽。

translations.literal: At first they planned to meet at Meng Ford; their hearts were set on Xianyang.
translations.idiomatic: At first they planned to meet at Meng Ford, their hearts set on Xianyang.

sentences.zh: 軍合力不齊，躊躇而雁行。

translations.literal: Armies joined but strength not aligned—hesitating, marching like wild geese in file.
translations.idiomatic: Their armies joined but their strength did not unite; they hesitated and marched in straggling lines.

sentences.zh: 勢利使人爭，嗣還自相戕。

translations.literal: Power and profit made men contend; heirs then turned to mutual slaughter.
translations.idiomatic: Ambition and profit drove them to quarrel, and soon they turned on one another.

sentences.zh: 淮南弟稱號，刻璽於北方。

translations.literal: The Huainan younger brother claimed a title, carving a seal in the north.
translations.idiomatic: The younger brother in Huainan claimed the throne, and another carved a seal in the north.

sentences.zh: 鎧甲生蟣蝨，萬姓以死亡。

translations.literal: Armor bred lice; the myriad clans thereby died.
translations.idiomatic: Armor bred lice, and the common people perished.

sentences.zh: 白骨露於野，千里無雞鳴。

translations.literal: White bones exposed in the wilds; for a thousand li, no cock's crow.
translations.idiomatic: White bones lay exposed in the fields; for a thousand leagues no cock crowed.

sentences.zh: 生民百遺一，念之絕人膓。

translations.literal: Of the living people, one in a hundred remained; thinking on it severs a man's entrails.
translations.idiomatic: Of all who lived, scarcely one in a hundred survived—to think of it tears the heart.

sentences.zh: 《對酒歌太平時》 《對酒》 武帝詞

translations.literal: "Facing Wine, Singing of Peaceful Times" / "Facing Wine" — lyrics by Emperor Wu
translations.idiomatic: "Facing Wine, Singing of Peaceful Times" (tune: "Facing Wine") — text by Emperor Wu of Wei

sentences.zh: 對酒歌，太平時，吏不呼門。

translations.literal: Facing wine, singing—peaceful times; clerks do not call at the door.
translations.idiomatic: Facing wine I sing of peaceful times, when clerks do not knock at the door.

sentences.zh: 王者賢且明，宰相股肱皆忠良，咸禮讓，民無所爭訟。

translations.literal: The king is worthy and enlightened; chancellors and arm-and-thigh ministers are all loyal and good; all practice courtesy and yielding; the people have nothing for which to quarrel and sue.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler is wise and enlightened, his ministers and chief aides are all loyal and upright, everyone observes ritual courtesy, and the people have no quarrels or lawsuits.

sentences.zh: 三年耕有九年儲，倉穀滿盈，斑白不負戴。

translations.literal: Three years' tilling yields nine years' stores; granary grain is full and overflowing; the gray-haired do not carry burdens on their backs.
translations.idiomatic: Three years of farming fill nine years of granaries; storehouses overflow with grain, and not even the gray-haired must bear loads on their backs.

translations.literal: Rain and moistening being like this, the five grains thereby are completed.
translations.idiomatic: With rains like these, the five grains ripen in plenty.

translations.literal: They turn back horses to manure their fields and soil.
translations.idiomatic: Warhorses are turned back to manure the fields.

sentences.zh: 爵公侯伯子男，咸愛其民，以黜陟幽明，子養有若父與兄。

translations.literal: The titled lords—duke, marquis, earl, viscount, and baron—all love their people, thereby dismissing and promoting, obscuring and clarifying; raising children as if father and elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Dukes, marquises, earls, viscounts, and barons all cherish their people, promoting the worthy and removing the unfit; in caring for their children they are like fathers and elder brothers.

translations.literal: Violating ritual and law, light or heavy accordingly their punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever breaks ritual or law is punished according to the gravity of the offense.

sentences.zh: 路無拾遺之私，囹圄空虛，冬節不斷人。

translations.literal: On the road there is no selfish picking up of lost things; prisons are empty and vacant; at the winter festival no cutting off of people.
translations.idiomatic: No one keeps what others have dropped; the prisons stand empty, and at the winter law court no one is put to death.

sentences.zh: 耄耋皆得以壽終，恩德廣及草木昆蟲。

translations.literal: The aged—eighty and ninety—all get to end in longevity; grace and virtue broadly reach grass, trees, insects, and creatures.
translations.idiomatic: Even the very aged complete their lives in peace, and royal kindness extends to grass, trees, and the smallest creatures.

translations.literal: "Rooster Crows atop the High Tree" / "Rooster Crows" — old lyrics
translations.idiomatic: "Rooster Crows atop the High Tree" (tune: "Rooster Crows") — traditional lyrics

sentences.zh: 雞鳴高樹顛，狗吠深宮中。

translations.literal: Rooster crows atop the high tree; dog barks in the deep palace.
translations.idiomatic: A rooster crows atop the high tree; a dog barks in the deep palace.

sentences.zh: 蕩子何所之，天下方太平。

translations.literal: The wandering son—where is he going? All under Heaven is just now at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Where is the wandering son going, when all under Heaven is at peace?

sentences.zh: 刑法非有貸，柔協正亂名。

translations.literal: Penal law is not lenient; gentleness and harmony correct disorderly reputations.
translations.idiomatic: The penal code knows no favoritism; only gentleness can set right a reputation for disorder.

sentences.zh: 黃金為君門，璧玉為軒堂。

translations.literal: Gold for the lord's gate; jade disks for the hall and chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Gold adorns the lord's gate; jade and fine disks decorate the hall.

sentences.zh: 上有雙尊酒，作使邯鄲倡。

translations.literal: Above are twin goblets of wine; employed are performers from Handan.
translations.idiomatic: Twin goblets of wine stand ready, and entertainers from Handan are summoned.

sentences.zh: 劉玉碧青甓，後出郭門王。

translations.literal: Fine jade, green-blue tiles; afterward going out the outer gate—the lord.
translations.idiomatic: Azure jade and green-blue tiles pave the halls; afterward the lord rides out through the outer gate.

sentences.zh: 舍後有方池，池中雙鴛鴦。

translations.literal: Behind the dwelling is a square pond; in the pond, a pair of mandarin ducks.
translations.idiomatic: Behind the house lies a square pond, and in the pond swim a pair of mandarin ducks.

sentences.zh: 鴛鴦七十二，羅列自成行。

translations.literal: Seventy-two mandarin ducks, arrayed in rows of their own.
translations.idiomatic: Seventy-two mandarin ducks line up in rows of their own.

sentences.zh: 鳴聲何啾啾，聞我殿東廂。

translations.literal: What chirping cries they make—hearing me in the east wing of the hall.
translations.idiomatic: How they chirp and call—hearing me in the east wing of the hall.

sentences.zh: 兄弟四五人，皆為侍中郎。

translations.literal: Four or five brothers, all are Attendants-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Four or five brothers, all holding posts as Attendants-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 五日一時來，觀者滿道傍。

translations.literal: Once every five days they come on schedule; spectators fill the roadside.
translations.idiomatic: Every five days they come on schedule, and spectators fill the roadside.

sentences.zh: 黃金絡馬頭，熲熲何煌煌。

translations.literal: Gold nets the horses' heads—how dazzling, how bright!
translations.idiomatic: Gold nets their horses' heads—how dazzling and bright!

sentences.zh: 桃生露井上，李樹生桃傍，蟲來齧桃根，李樹代桃僵。

translations.literal: Peach grows atop the open well; plum tree grows beside the peach; worms come and gnaw the peach roots; the plum tree dies in the peach's place.
translations.idiomatic: A peach grows atop the open well, a plum beside it; when worms gnaw the peach roots, the plum tree withers in the peach's stead.

sentences.zh: 樹木身相代，兄弟還相忘！

translations.literal: Trees may substitute for one another in body—yet brothers still forget each other!
translations.idiomatic: Trees may die in one another's place, yet brothers still forget each other!

translations.literal: "Crow Born with Eight or Nine Young" / "Crow Born" — old lyrics
translations.idiomatic: "Crow Born with Eight or Nine Young" (tune: "Crow Born") — traditional lyrics

sentences.zh: 烏生八九子，端坐秦氏桂樹間。

translations.literal: Crow born with eight or nine young, sitting upright among the Qin family's cassia trees.
translations.idiomatic: A crow has borne eight or nine young and sits upright among the Qin family's cassia trees.

sentences.zh: 唶我秦氏，家有游遨蕩子，工用睢陽強蘇合彈。

translations.literal: Alas, my Qin family—there is a roaming wastrel who skillfully uses a powerful Suiyang slingshot with storax-compounded pellets.
translations.idiomatic: Alas, in our Qin household lives a roaming wastrel who skillfully wields a powerful Suiyang slingshot loaded with storax-hardened pellets.

sentences.zh: 左手持強彈，兩丸出入烏東西。

translations.literal: In his left hand he holds the powerful slingshot; two pellets fly east and west around the crow.
translations.idiomatic: In his left hand he holds the powerful slingshot; two pellets fly back and forth around the crow.

sentences.zh: 唶我一丸即發中烏身，烏死魂魄飛揚上天。

translations.literal: Alas—one pellet fired strikes the crow's body; the crow dies and its soul soars upward to heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Alas—one pellet fired strikes the crow; the bird dies and its soul soars up to heaven.

sentences.zh: 阿母生烏子時，乃在南山巖石間。

translations.literal: When mother crow bore her young, it was among the rocks of South Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: When mother crow bore her young, she nested among the rocks of South Mountain.

sentences.zh: 唶我人民安知烏子處，蹊徑窈窕安從通。

translations.literal: Alas, how could people know where the young crows are? The hidden path is winding—how could one reach them?
translations.idiomatic: Alas, how could anyone know where the young crows hide? The hidden path is winding—how could one ever reach them?

sentences.zh: 白鹿乃在上林西苑中，射工尚復得白鹿脯。

translations.literal: A white deer lives in Shanglin's Western Park, yet even hunters can still get white deer jerky.
translations.idiomatic: A white deer lives in Shanglin's Western Park, yet even hunters can still get white deer jerky.

sentences.zh: 唶我黃鵠摩天極高飛，後宮尚復得亨煑之。

translations.literal: Alas—a yellow swan flies soaring to the sky's edge; even the rear palace can still boil and stew it.
translations.idiomatic: Alas—a yellow swan soars to the sky's edge, yet even the rear palace can still boil and stew it.

sentences.zh: 鯉魚乃在洛水深淵中，釣鉤尚得鯉魚口。

translations.literal: Carp dwell in Luoyang River's deep abyss, yet fishing hooks still catch the carp in the mouth.
translations.idiomatic: Carp dwell in the deep pools of the Luo River, yet fishing hooks still catch them in the mouth.

sentences.zh: 唶我人民生各各有壽命，死生何須復道前後。

translations.literal: Alas, people each have their own allotted span of life—what need to speak of before and after in death and life?
translations.idiomatic: Alas, each person has an allotted span of life—what need to speak of before and after in death and life?

translations.literal: "East of Pingling" / "Pingling" — old lyrics
translations.idiomatic: "East of Pingling" (tune: "Pingling") — traditional lyrics

sentences.zh: 平陵東，松栢桐，不知何人劫義公。

translations.literal: East of Pingling, pine, cypress, and paulownia—I know not who robbed Lord Yi.
translations.idiomatic: East of Pingling, among pine, cypress, and paulownia—I know not who robbed Lord Yi.

sentences.zh: 劫義公在高堂下，交錢百萬兩走馬。

translations.literal: They robbed Lord Yi beneath the high hall; hand over a million in cash and two horses.
translations.idiomatic: They robbed Lord Yi beneath the high hall; hand over a million in cash and two horses.

sentences.zh: 兩走馬，亦誠難，顧見追吏心中惻。

translations.literal: Two horses—that is truly hard; turning to look at the pursuing officers, the heart aches within.
translations.idiomatic: Two horses—that is truly hard to give; turning to see the pursuing officers, my heart aches within.

sentences.zh: 心中惻，血出漉，歸告我家賣黃犢。

translations.literal: The heart aches within; blood oozes and drips; return home and tell my family to sell the yellow calf.
translations.idiomatic: My heart aches within and blood oozes forth; go home and tell my family to sell the yellow calf.

translations.literal: "Abandoning Homeland"
translations.idiomatic: "Abandoning Homeland"

translations.literal: (Also in the se-tuning "East-West Gate Song")
translations.idiomatic: (Also set to the se-mode tune "East-West Gate Song")

translations.literal: "Mulberry by the Road" — lyrics by Emperor Wen
translations.idiomatic: "Mulberry by the Road" — text by Emperor Wen of Wei

sentences.zh: 棄故鄉，離室宅，遠從軍旅萬里客。

translations.literal: Abandoning homeland, leaving dwelling and house, far following the army and host—a traveler ten thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: I abandoned my homeland and left my dwelling, following the army far away as a traveler ten thousand li from home.

sentences.zh: 披荊棘，求阡陌，側足獨窘步，路局笮。

translations.literal: Pushing through brambles, seeking paths and lanes; stepping sideways, alone and in straits; the road is narrow and cramped.
translations.idiomatic: Pushing through brambles, seeking paths and lanes, I step sideways alone in straits—the road is narrow and cramped.

sentences.zh: 虎豹嗥動，雞驚，禽失羣，鳴相索。

translations.literal: Tigers and leopards howl and stir; chickens startle; birds lose their flocks and cry, calling to one another.
translations.idiomatic: Tigers and leopards howl and prowl; chickens startle; birds lose their flocks and cry, calling to one another.

sentences.zh: 登南山，奈何蹈槃石，樹木叢生鬱差錯。

translations.literal: Climbing South Mountain—alas, treading on boulders; trees grow thick and tangled in luxuriant confusion.
translations.idiomatic: I climb South Mountain—alas, treading on boulders; trees grow thick and tangled in luxuriant confusion.

sentences.zh: 寢蒿草，蔭松栢，涕泣雨面霑枕席。

translations.literal: Lying on wild mugwort, shaded by pine and cypress; tears rain on the face and soak pillow and mat.
translations.idiomatic: I lie on wild mugwort, shaded by pine and cypress; tears rain on my face and soak my pillow and mat.

sentences.zh: 伴旅單，稍稍日零落，惆悵竊自憐，相痛惜。

translations.literal: Alone with a traveling companion, day by day gradually dwindling; despondency steals upon me and I pity myself—we ache for each other.
translations.idiomatic: Alone with my traveling companion, day by day we dwindle; despondency steals upon me and I pity myself—we ache for each other.

translations.literal: "There Is a Man" / "Mulberry by the Road" / excerpt from Songs of Chu
translations.idiomatic: "There Is a Man" (tune: "Mulberry by the Road") — excerpted from the Songs of Chu

sentences.zh: 今有人，山之阿，被服薜荔帶女蘿。

translations.literal: There is a man on the mountain slope, clad in cassia vine and girdled with maidenwort.
translations.idiomatic: There is someone on the mountain slope, clad in cassia vine and girdled with maidenwort.

sentences.zh: 既含睇，又宜笑，子戀慕予善窈窕。

translations.literal: She has a sidelong glance and a smile that suits her; you, sir, gaze in longing at my fair grace.
translations.idiomatic: She has a sidelong glance and a smile that suits her; you, sir, gaze in longing at my fair grace.

sentences.zh: 乘赤豹，從文貍，新夷車駕結桂旗。

translations.literal: Riding a red leopard, following striped civets, in a fresh-wood chariot harnessed with cassia banners tied.
translations.idiomatic: Riding a red leopard, following striped civets, in a chariot of fresh-cut wood with cassia banners tied.

sentences.zh: 被石蘭，帶杜衡，折芳拔荃遺所思。

translations.literal: Clad in stone orchid, girdled with wild angelica—breaking fragrant herbs and pulling up iris to leave for the one I love.
translations.idiomatic: Clad in stone orchid, girdled with wild angelica—breaking fragrant herbs and pulling up iris to leave for the one I love.

sentences.zh: 處幽室，終不見，天路險艱獨後來。

translations.literal: Dwelling in a hidden chamber, at last unseen; the road to heaven is perilous—alone I come afterward.
translations.idiomatic: Dwelling in a hidden chamber, at last unseen; the road to heaven is perilous—I come afterward alone.

sentences.zh: 表獨立，山之上，雲何容容而在下。

translations.literal: Standing alone displayed on the mountain crest—why do the clouds gather so thickly below?
translations.idiomatic: Standing alone atop the mountain—why do the clouds gather so thickly below?

sentences.zh: 杳冥冥，羌晝晦，東風飄颻神靈雨。

translations.literal: Distant and dark, even day is dim; the east wind sways and a spirit rain falls.
translations.idiomatic: Distant and dark, even day is dim; the east wind sways and a spirit rain falls.

sentences.zh: 風瑟瑟，木搜搜，思念公子徒以憂。

translations.literal: Wind sighs; trees rustle; thinking of the prince, I can only mourn in vain.
translations.idiomatic: The wind sighs; the trees rustle; thinking of the prince, I can only mourn in vain.

translations.literal: "Driving the Rainbow" / "Mulberry by the Road" — lyrics by Emperor Wu
translations.idiomatic: "Driving the Rainbow" (tune: "Mulberry by the Road") — text by Emperor Wu of Wei

sentences.zh: 駕虹蜺，乘赤雲，登彼九疑歷王門。

translations.literal: Driving the rainbow, riding scarlet clouds, ascending those Nine Mounds and passing through the King's Gate.
translations.idiomatic: I drive the rainbow and ride scarlet clouds, ascending the Nine Mounds and passing through the King's Gate.

sentences.zh: 濟天漢，至崐崘，見西王母，謁東君。

translations.literal: Crossing the Heavenly River, reaching Kunlun, seeing the Queen Mother of the West, paying court to the Lord of the East.
translations.idiomatic: I cross the Heavenly River and reach Kunlun, see the Queen Mother of the West, and pay court to the Lord of the East.

sentences.zh: 交赤松，及羨門，受要秘道愛精神。

translations.literal: Meeting Red Pine and Xianmen, receiving the essential secret Way and cherishing the spirit.
translations.idiomatic: I meet Red Pine and Xianmen, receive the essential secret Way, and cherish my spirit.

sentences.zh: 食芝英，飲醴泉，柱杖桂枝佩秋蘭。

translations.literal: Eating mushroom essence, drinking sweet spring wine, leaning on a cane of cassia branch and wearing autumn orchid at the belt.
translations.idiomatic: I eat mushroom essence and drink sweet spring wine, lean on a cassia cane, and wear autumn orchid at my belt.

sentences.zh: 絕人事，游渾元，若疾風游歘飄飄。

translations.literal: Cutting off from human affairs, roaming in primal chaos, like a fierce wind rushing—swift and fluttering.
translations.idiomatic: I cut off from human affairs and roam in primal chaos, like a fierce wind rushing—swift and fluttering.

sentences.zh: 景未移，行數千，壽如南山不忘愆。

translations.literal: The scene has not shifted; I have traveled thousands of miles—long life like South Mountain, never forgetting fault.
translations.idiomatic: The scene has barely changed yet I have traveled thousands of miles—long life like South Mountain, never forgetting my faults.

sentences.zh: 清商三調歌詩 荀勖撰，舊詞施用者

translations.literal: Qing Shang three-tune song lyrics — composed by Xun Xu; old lyrics still used
translations.idiomatic: Qing Shang Three-Tune Song Lyrics — composed by Xun Xu; traditional lyrics still in use

translations.literal: "Zhou West" / "Short Song Ballad" — lyrics by Emperor Wu
translations.idiomatic: "Zhou West" (tune: "Short Song Ballad") — text by Emperor Wu of Wei

translations.literal: Section Six
translations.idiomatic: Section Six

sentences.zh: 周西伯昌，懷此聖德，參分天下，而有其二。

translations.literal: Duke Wen of the West, Chang, held this sagely virtue; the realm was divided into three parts, and he held two of them.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Wen of Zhou, Chang, held this sagely virtue; though the realm was divided into three parts, he held two of them.

translations.literal: He reverently offered tribute and gifts; ministerial rectitude did not fall.
translations.idiomatic: He reverently offered tribute and gifts, and his ministerial duty never lapsed.

translations.literal: Chong Hou slandered him, and for this he was imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Chong Hou slandered him, and for this he was imprisoned.

translations.literal: Section One
translations.idiomatic: Section One

sentences.zh: 後見赦原，賜之斧鉞，得使征伐。

translations.literal: Later he was pardoned and restored; given axe and halberd, permitted to go on campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was pardoned and restored, given axe and halberd, and permitted to go on campaign.

sentences.zh: 為仲尼所稱，達及德行，猶奉事殷，論叙其美。

translations.literal: Praised by Confucius, reaching to virtue and conduct—still he served the Yin, narrating its excellence.
translations.idiomatic: Praised by Confucius for his virtue and conduct, he still served the Yin and recounted its excellence.

translations.literal: Section Two
translations.idiomatic: Section Two

sentences.zh: 齊桓之功，為霸之首，九合諸侯，一匡天下。

translations.literal: Duke Huan of Qi's achievement—first among hegemons; nine times he assembled the lords, once he set the realm in order.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Huan of Qi's achievement was first among the hegemons: nine times he assembled the lords and once set the realm in order.

translations.literal: Once he set the realm in order—without relying on chariots of war.
translations.idiomatic: He set the realm in order without relying on chariots of war.

translations.literal: Upright and not deceitful—his virtue is praised in tradition.
translations.idiomatic: Upright and not deceitful—his virtue is praised in tradition.

translations.literal: Section Three
translations.idiomatic: Section Three

sentences.zh: 孔子所歎，并稱夷吾，民受其恩。

translations.literal: What Confucius admired—he praised Guan Zhong together; the people received his grace.
translations.idiomatic: What Confucius admired—he praised Guan Zhong alongside him, and the people received his grace.

translations.literal: Granted temple sacrificial meat; ordered that he need not bow.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted temple sacrificial meat and ordered that he need not bow.

sentences.zh: 小白不敢爾，天威在顏咫尺。

translations.literal: Duke Huan dared not do so—the Heavenly Majesty was within a foot of his face.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Huan dared not do so—the Heavenly Majesty was within a foot of his face.

translations.literal: Section Four
translations.idiomatic: Section Four

translations.literal: Duke Wen of Jin also achieved hegemony, personally serving the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Wen of Jin also achieved hegemony, personally serving the Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 受賜珪瓚、秬鬯彤弓、盧弓、矢千，虎賁三百人。

translations.literal: He received gifts of sacrificial jade goblet, black millet wine, red bow, black bow, a thousand arrows, and three hundred tiger guards.
translations.idiomatic: He received gifts of a sacrificial jade goblet, black millet wine, a red bow, a black bow, a thousand arrows, and three hundred tiger guards.

translations.literal: Section Five
translations.idiomatic: Section Five

sentences.zh: 威服諸侯，師之者尊，八方聞之，名亞齊桓。

translations.literal: By might he brought the lords to submission—those who took him as teacher were honored; all eight directions heard of him; his name ranked second to Duke Huan's.
translations.idiomatic: By might he brought the lords to submission; those who took him as their model were honored; all eight directions heard of him, and his name ranked second to Duke Huan's.

sentences.zh: 河陽之會，詐稱周王，是以其名紛葩。

translations.literal: At the meeting at Heyang he falsely claimed the title of King of Zhou—hence his reputation is mixed and disputed.
translations.idiomatic: At the meeting at Heyang he falsely claimed the title of King of Zhou—hence his reputation is mixed and disputed.

translations.literal: Section Six
translations.idiomatic: Section Six

translations.literal: "Autumn Wind" / "Swallow Song Ballad" — lyrics by Emperor Wen
translations.idiomatic: "Autumn Wind" (tune: "Swallow Song Ballad") — text by Emperor Wen of Wei

translations.literal: Section Seven
translations.idiomatic: Section Seven

sentences.zh: 秋風蕭瑟天氣涼，草木搖落露為霜。

translations.literal: The autumn wind is sighing; the weather grows cold; grass and trees shiver and drop; dew turns to frost.
translations.idiomatic: The autumn wind sighs and the weather turns cold; grass and trees shiver and drop, and dew turns to frost.

translations.literal: Section One
translations.idiomatic: Section One

sentences.zh: 羣燕辭歸鵠南翔，念君客游多思腸。

translations.literal: Flocks of swallows leave and wild geese fly south; thinking of you traveling far, my thoughts fill with longing.
translations.idiomatic: Flocks of swallows depart and wild geese fly south; thinking of you traveling far, my thoughts fill with longing.

translations.literal: Section Two
translations.idiomatic: Section Two

sentences.zh: 慊慊思歸戀故鄉，君何淹留寄它方。

translations.literal: Restless, I long for home and miss my old country—why do you linger, staying in another land?
translations.idiomatic: Restless, I long for home and miss my old country—why do you linger, staying in another land?

translations.literal: Section Three
translations.idiomatic: Section Three

sentences.zh: 賤妾煢煢守空房，憂來思君不敢忘。

translations.literal: I, your humble wife, alone keep to the empty chamber; sorrow comes and thoughts of you—I dare not forget.
translations.idiomatic: I, your humble wife, alone keep to the empty chamber; sorrow comes and thoughts of you—I dare not forget.

translations.literal: Section Four
translations.idiomatic: Section Four

sentences.zh: 不覺淚下霑衣裳，援瑟鳴弦發清商。

translations.literal: Before I know it, tears fall and soak my robes; I take up the zither, pluck the strings, and play in clear Shang mode.
translations.idiomatic: Before I know it, tears fall and soak my robes; I take up the zither, pluck the strings, and play in the clear Shang mode.

translations.literal: Section Five
translations.idiomatic: Section Five

sentences.zh: 短歌微吟不能長，明月皎皎照我床。

translations.literal: Short song, softly chanted, cannot be long; the bright moon shines clear upon my bed.
translations.idiomatic: My short song, softly chanted, cannot run long; the bright moon shines clear upon my bed.

translations.literal: Section Six
translations.idiomatic: Section Six

sentences.zh: 星漢西流夜未央，牽年織女遙相望，爾獨何辜限河梁。

translations.literal: The River of Stars flows west; the night is not yet half done; Oxherd and Weaver Girl gaze at each other from afar—why alone do you suffer, barred by the River Bridge?
translations.idiomatic: The Milky Way flows westward; the night is far from done; the Cowherd and Weaver Girl gaze at each other across the void—why alone must you suffer, parted by the Bridge of Stars?

translations.literal: Section Seven
translations.idiomatic: Section Seven

translations.literal: "Gazing Upward" / "Short Song Ballad" — lyrics by Emperor Wen
translations.idiomatic: "Gazing Upward" (tune: "Short Song Ballad") — text by Emperor Wen of Wei

translations.literal: Section Six
translations.idiomatic: Section Six

translations.literal: Looking up, I gaze at the curtain-canopy; looking down, I inspect the mat and table.
translations.idiomatic: I look up at the curtain-canopy and down at the mat and table.

translations.literal: The things are as before; the person is no more.
translations.idiomatic: The things remain as they were; the man is gone.

translations.literal: Section One
translations.idiomatic: Section One

translations.literal: The spirit, in a flash, abandoned me and went far away.
translations.idiomatic: His spirit, in an instant, left me and went far away.

translations.literal: No longer to look upon, no longer to rely upon—tears stream unceasing.
translations.idiomatic: No longer to behold, no longer to lean upon—my tears fall without end.

translations.literal: Section Two
translations.idiomatic: Section Two

translations.literal: Yo-yo, the roaming deer, carries grass and calls its fawn.
translations.idiomatic: The deer roam, lowing; they carry grass and call their fawns.

translations.literal: Fluttering birds carry their young back to the nest to roost.
translations.idiomatic: Birds wheel and flutter, bearing their young home to the nest.

translations.literal: Section Three
translations.idiomatic: Section Three

translations.literal: I alone am forsaken and desolate, bearing these hundred partings.
translations.idiomatic: I alone am forsaken and desolate, burdened with a hundred griefs of parting.

translations.literal: My heart is deeply anguished—none can understand me.
translations.idiomatic: My heart is deeply anguished—no one can know what I feel.

translations.literal: Section Four
translations.idiomatic: Section Four

translations.literal: People also say: sorrow makes one old.
translations.idiomatic: People say that sorrow ages a man.

translations.literal: Alas, my white hair—how early it came!
translations.idiomatic: Alas—my white hair! How early it came.

translations.literal: Section Five
translations.idiomatic: Section Five

translations.literal: Long singing, eternal sighing—I mourn my sage father.
translations.idiomatic: Long I sing and long I sigh, mourning my revered father.

translations.literal: They say the benevolent live long—why was he not preserved?
translations.idiomatic: They say the benevolent live long—why was he not spared?

translations.literal: Section Six
translations.idiomatic: Section Six

translations.literal: "Parting Day" / "Swallow Song Ballad" — lyrics by Emperor Wen
translations.idiomatic: "Parting Day" (tune: "Swallow Song Ballad") — text by Emperor Wen of Wei

translations.literal: Section Six
translations.idiomatic: Section Six

sentences.zh: 別日何易會日難，山川悠遠路漫漫。

translations.literal: Parting is so easy; meeting again is hard—mountains and rivers stretch far, the road endless.
translations.idiomatic: Parting comes so easily; meeting again is hard—mountains and rivers stretch endlessly, the road without end.

translations.literal: Section One
translations.idiomatic: Section One

sentences.zh: 鬱陶思君未敢言，寄書浮雲往不還。

translations.literal: Distressed, I think of you but dare not speak; I send a letter—it rides the drifting clouds and does not return.
translations.idiomatic: Distressed with longing, I think of you yet dare not speak; I send a letter—it rides the drifting clouds and never returns.

translations.literal: Section Two
translations.idiomatic: Section Two

sentences.zh: 涕零雨面毀形顏，誰能懷憂獨不歎。

translations.literal: Tears fall like rain and ruin my face—who can harbor sorrow and not sigh alone?
translations.idiomatic: Tears fall like rain and mar my face—who can bear such sorrow and not sigh?

translations.literal: Section Three
translations.idiomatic: Section Three

sentences.zh: 耿耿伏枕不能眠，披衣出戶步東西。

translations.literal: Restless, I lie on my pillow and cannot sleep; I throw on my robe, go out the door, and pace east and west.
translations.idiomatic: Restless, I lie on my pillow and cannot sleep; I throw on my robe, go out the door, and pace to and fro.

translations.literal: Section Four
translations.idiomatic: Section Four

sentences.zh: 展詩清歌聊自寬，樂往哀來摧心肝。

translations.literal: I unfold my poem and sing a clear song to ease myself awhile; joy departs and sorrow comes, crushing heart and liver.
translations.idiomatic: I unfold my poem and sing a clear song to comfort myself awhile; joy departs and sorrow arrives, crushing my heart.

sentences.zh: 悲風清厲秋氣寒，羅帷徐動經秦軒。

translations.literal: The mournful wind blows sharp and clear; autumn air is cold; silk curtains stir slowly, passing the Qin-style gallery.
translations.idiomatic: The mournful wind blows sharp and cold; autumn chills the air; silk curtains stir slowly along the gallery rail.

translations.literal: Section Five
translations.idiomatic: Section Five

sentences.zh: 仰戴星月觀雲間，飛鳥晨鳴，聲氣可憐，留連顧懷不自存。

translations.literal: Looking up I behold the stars and moon and watch the clouds; morning birds cry—their voices touch the heart; lingering, I turn and look back, unable to contain myself.
translations.idiomatic: I look up at the stars and moon and watch the clouds; birds cry at dawn—their voices pierce the heart; lingering, I turn and look back, unable to hold myself together.

translations.literal: Section Six
translations.idiomatic: Section Six

translations.literal: "Facing Wine" / "Short Song Ballad" — lyrics by Emperor Wu
translations.idiomatic: "Facing Wine" (tune: "Short Song Ballad") — text by Emperor Wu of Wei

translations.literal: Section Six
translations.idiomatic: Section Six

translations.literal: Facing wine, I should sing—how long is human life!
translations.idiomatic: Facing wine, I should sing—how brief is human life!

translations.literal: Like morning dew; days gone are painfully many.
translations.idiomatic: Like morning dew; the days already gone are painfully many.

translations.literal: Section One
translations.idiomatic: Section One

translations.literal: When generous feeling should rise, anxious thoughts are hard to forget.
translations.idiomatic: When generous feeling should rise, anxious thoughts are hard to put aside.

translations.literal: With what to dispel sorrow? Only Duke Kang wine.
translations.idiomatic: What can dispel this sorrow? Only Duke Kang wine.

translations.literal: Section Two
translations.idiomatic: Section Two

translations.literal: Green, green your collar-hem; long, long my heart.
translations.idiomatic: Green, green your collar; long, long my heart.

translations.literal: But for your sake, I have pondered until now.
translations.idiomatic: But for your sake, I have lingered in thought until now.

translations.literal: Section Three
translations.idiomatic: Section Three

translations.literal: Bright, bright like the moon—when can I pluck it down?
translations.idiomatic: Bright as the moon—when can I grasp it?

translations.literal: Sorrow comes from within; it cannot be cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Sorrow rises from within and cannot be severed.

translations.literal: Section Four
translations.idiomatic: Section Four

translations.literal: Yo-yo, the deer call; they eat the wild duckweed.
translations.idiomatic: The deer call, lowing; they graze on the wild duckweed.

translations.literal: I have honored guests; I strum the zither and blow the pipes.
translations.idiomatic: I have honored guests; I strum the zither and sound the pipes.

translations.literal: Section Five
translations.idiomatic: Section Five

translations.literal: Mountains do not dislike height; waters do not dislike depth.
translations.idiomatic: Mountains do not disdain their height; waters do not disdain their depth.

translations.literal: The Duke of Zhou spat out his meal; all under Heaven turned their hearts to him.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Zhou spat out a mouthful of his meal; all under Heaven gave him their hearts.

translations.literal: Section Six
translations.idiomatic: Section Six

translations.literal: "Morning Ascent" / "Autumn Hu Ballad" — lyrics by Emperor Wu
translations.idiomatic: "Morning Ascent" (tune: "Autumn Hu Ballad") — text by Emperor Wu of Wei

sentences.zh: 晨上散關山，此道當何難！

translations.literal: At dawn I ascend San Pass Mountain—how hard should this road be!
translations.idiomatic: At dawn I climb San Pass Mountain—how hard can this road be!

sentences.zh: 晨上散關山，此道當何難！

translations.literal: At dawn I ascend San Pass Mountain—how hard should this road be!
translations.idiomatic: At dawn I climb San Pass Mountain—how hard can this road be!

translations.literal: The ox refuses to rise; the cart falls into the ravine.
translations.idiomatic: The ox will not rise; the cart tumbles into the ravine.

sentences.zh: 坐盤石之上，彈五弦之琴，作為清角韻，意中述煩。

translations.literal: Sitting on a flat rock, I pluck a five-string zither, playing in clear jue mode, voicing the troubles in my heart.
translations.idiomatic: I sit on a flat rock and pluck a five-string zither, playing in clear jue mode to voice the troubles in my heart.

translations.literal: I sing to declare my intent: at dawn ascending San Pass Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: I sing to declare my intent: at dawn, ascending San Pass Mountain.

translations.literal: Section One
translations.idiomatic: Section One

sentences.zh: 有何三老公，卒來在我傍。

translations.literal: What three old men, suddenly coming beside me!
translations.idiomatic: What three old men, suddenly appearing beside me!

sentences.zh: 有何三老公，卒來在我傍。

translations.literal: What three old men, suddenly coming beside me!
translations.idiomatic: What three old men, suddenly appearing beside me!

translations.literal: Round-capped, wrapped in fur robes—they do not seem ordinary men.
translations.idiomatic: Round-capped, wrapped in fur robes—they do not seem like ordinary men.

sentences.zh: 謂卿云何，困苦以自怨，徨徨所欲，來到此間。

translations.literal: They said: "Why do you, sir, torment yourself with complaint? What you wander in search of has brought you to this place."
translations.idiomatic: "Why, sir," they said, "do you torment yourself with complaint? What you wander in search of has brought you here."

translations.literal: I sing to declare my intent: what three old men.
translations.idiomatic: I sing to declare my intent: what three old men.

translations.literal: Section Two
translations.idiomatic: Section Two

sentences.zh: 我居崐崘山，所謂者真人。

translations.literal: I dwell on Mount Kunlun—what they call a true man.
translations.idiomatic: I dwell on Mount Kunlun—they call me a true man.

sentences.zh: 我居崐崘山，所謂者真人。

translations.literal: I dwell on Mount Kunlun—what they call a true man.
translations.idiomatic: I dwell on Mount Kunlun—they call me a true man.

translations.literal: The Way is deep; one may attain it.
translations.idiomatic: The Way runs deep; one may attain it.

translations.literal: Visit famous mountains, roam the eight extremities.
translations.idiomatic: Visit famous mountains and roam the eight extremities.

translations.literal: Pillowing on stone, rinsing with flowing water, drinking from springs.
translations.idiomatic: Pillow on stone, rinse in running water, drink from springs.

translations.literal: Hesitating, unable to decide—then ascending to heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Hesitating, unable to decide—then ascending to heaven.

translations.literal: I sing to declare my intent: I dwell on Mount Kunlun.
translations.idiomatic: I sing to declare my intent: I dwell on Mount Kunlun.

translations.literal: Section Three
translations.idiomatic: Section Three

sentences.zh: 去去不可追，長恨相牽攀。

translations.literal: Gone, gone—cannot be pursued; long regret mutually entangled.
translations.idiomatic: Gone, gone—beyond pursuit; long regret holds us bound together.

sentences.zh: 去去不可追，長恨相牽攀。

translations.literal: Gone, gone—cannot be pursued; long regret mutually entangled.
translations.idiomatic: Gone, gone—beyond pursuit; long regret holds us bound together.

sentences.zh: 夜夜安得寐，惆悵以自憐。

translations.literal: Night after night, how can I sleep? Desolate, I pity myself.
translations.idiomatic: Night after night, how can I sleep? Desolate, I pity myself.

translations.literal: Upright and not deceitful; rhymes and fu follow the pattern.
translations.idiomatic: Upright and not deceitful; the verses follow their model.

translations.literal: What the classics and commentaries pass down, what came transmitted from the west.
translations.idiomatic: What the classics and commentaries pass down, what came transmitted from the west.

translations.literal: I sing to declare my intent: gone, gone—cannot be pursued.
translations.idiomatic: I sing to declare my intent: gone, gone—beyond pursuit.

translations.literal: Section Four.
translations.idiomatic: Section Four.

sentences.zh: 又本：晨‖上‖散‖關‖山‖，此‖道‖當‖何‖難。

translations.literal: Another version: At dawn I ascend San Pass Mountain—how hard should this road be.
translations.idiomatic: Alternate version: At dawn I climb San Pass Mountain—how hard can this road be.

sentences.zh: 有‖何‖三‖老‖公，卒‖來‖在‖我‖傍‖。

translations.literal: What three old men, suddenly coming beside me.
translations.idiomatic: What three old men, suddenly appearing beside me.

sentences.zh: 我‖居‖我‖崐‖崘‖山‖，所‖謂‖真‖人‖，去‖不‖可‖追‖，長‖相‖牽‖攀‖。〉

translations.literal: I dwell on Mount Kunlun, called a true man; gone, cannot be pursued; long mutual entanglement.
translations.idiomatic: I dwell on Mount Kunlun, called a true man; gone, beyond pursuit; long bound together in regret.

translations.literal: "Northward Journey" / "Bitter Cold Journey" — lyrics by Emperor Wu
translations.idiomatic: "Northward Journey" (tune: "Bitter Cold Journey") — text by Emperor Wu of Wei

translations.literal: Section Six
translations.idiomatic: Section Six

sentences.zh: 北上太‖行‖山‖，艱‖哉‖何‖巍巍。

translations.literal: Northward up Mount Tai‖hang‖—how steep and towering!
translations.idiomatic: Northward up Mount Taihang—how steep and towering!

sentences.zh: 羊腸阪詰屈，車輪為之摧。

translations.literal: Sheep-Gut Slope winds tortuously; chariot wheels are shattered by it.
translations.idiomatic: Sheep-Gut Slope winds tortuously; chariot wheels are shattered on it.

translations.literal: Section One
translations.idiomatic: Section One

sentences.zh: 樹木何蕭‖瑟‖，北‖風‖聲‖正‖悲‖。

translations.literal: How sighing the trees; the north wind's voice is truly mournful.
translations.idiomatic: The trees sigh; the north wind's voice is truly mournful.

sentences.zh: 熊羆對我蹲，虎豹夾道啼。

translations.literal: Bears and badgers crouch facing me; tigers and leopards line the road, howling.
translations.idiomatic: Bears and badgers crouch before me; tigers and leopards line the road, howling.

translations.literal: Section Two
translations.idiomatic: Section Two

sentences.zh: 溪穀少‖人‖民‖，雪‖落‖何‖霏‖霏‖。

translations.literal: In the valleys few are the people; how thickly the snow falls.
translations.idiomatic: In the valleys people are few; how thickly the snow falls.

sentences.zh: 延頸長歎息，遠行多所懷。

translations.literal: I stretch my neck and sigh long; on a distant journey, many things fill my heart.
translations.idiomatic: I stretch my neck and sigh long; on this distant journey, many things fill my heart.

translations.literal: Section Three
translations.idiomatic: Section Three

sentences.zh: 我心何‖佛‖鬱‖，思‖欲‖一‖東‖歸‖。

translations.literal: Why is my heart so vexed and depressed? I long to return east at once.
translations.idiomatic: Why is my heart so vexed and heavy? I long to turn homeward east at once.

sentences.zh: 水深橋梁絕，中道正裴回。

translations.literal: The waters run deep and bridges are cut off; midway I turn and linger.
translations.idiomatic: The waters run deep and the bridges are gone; halfway there I turn and linger.

translations.literal: Section Four
translations.idiomatic: Section Four

sentences.zh: 迷惑失‖徑‖路‖，暝‖無‖所‖宿‖棲‖。

translations.literal: Lost and confused, I lose the path; at dusk there is no place to lodge.
translations.idiomatic: Bewildered, I lose the trail; at dusk I have nowhere to rest.

sentences.zh: 行行日以遠，人馬同時飢。

translations.literal: Step by step the days grow distant; men and horses hunger together.
translations.idiomatic: Step by step the days recede; men and horses hunger alike.

translations.literal: Section Five
translations.idiomatic: Section Five

sentences.zh: 儋‖囊‖行‖取‖薪‖，斧‖冰‖持‖作‖糜‖。

translations.literal: Shouldering a bag, I go to gather firewood; I chop ice and make gruel.
translations.idiomatic: Bag on my shoulder, I go for firewood; I hew ice and boil it into gruel.

sentences.zh: 悲彼東山詩，悠悠使我哀。

translations.literal: I grieve at that poem of the Eastern Hills; its long sorrow fills me with grief.
translations.idiomatic: That poem of the Eastern Hills fills me with grief; its long sorrow pierces me.

translations.literal: Section Six
translations.idiomatic: Section Six

translations.literal: "Longing to Ascend" / "Autumn Hu Ballad" — lyrics by Emperor Wu
translations.idiomatic: "Longing to Ascend" (tune: "Autumn Hu Ballad") — text by Emperor Wu of Wei

translations.literal: Section Five
translations.idiomatic: Section Five

sentences.zh: 願‖登‖泰‖華‖山‖，神‖人‖共‖遠‖游‖。

translations.literal: I wish to climb Mount Taihua and roam far with the immortals.
translations.idiomatic: I long to climb Mount Taihua and wander far with the immortals.

translations.literal: Passing Mount Kunlun, arriving at Penglai.
translations.idiomatic: Passing Mount Kunlun, I would reach Penglai.

translations.literal: Drifting through the eight extremities, together with divine beings.
translations.idiomatic: I would drift through the eight reaches of the world, side by side with the immortals.

translations.literal: I think to obtain divine elixir, with ten thousand years as my term.
translations.idiomatic: I dream of divine elixir, with ten thousand years as my span.

translations.literal: I sing to declare my intent: I long to climb Mount Taihua.
translations.idiomatic: I sing to declare my intent: to climb Mount Taihua.

translations.literal: Section One
translations.idiomatic: Section One

sentences.zh: 天‖地‖何‖長‖久‖，人‖道‖居‖之‖短‖。

translations.literal: How enduring are Heaven and Earth; how brief is the human way.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and Earth endure forever; man's span is brief.

sentences.zh: 世言伯陽，殊不知老，赤松王喬，亦云得道。

translations.literal: The world speaks of Boyang, yet knows nothing of Laozi; Chisong and Wang Qiao, too, are said to have attained the Way.
translations.idiomatic: The world speaks of Boyang, yet knows nothing of Laozi; Chisong and Wang Qiao, too, are said to have attained the Way.

translations.literal: That one has obtained it I have never heard; perhaps one may reach old age.
translations.idiomatic: I have never heard of anyone who truly obtained it; perhaps one may still live out a full span.

translations.literal: I sing to declare my intent: how enduring are Heaven and Earth!
translations.idiomatic: I sing to declare my intent: how enduring are Heaven and Earth!

translations.literal: Section Two
translations.idiomatic: Section Two

sentences.zh: 明‖明‖日‖月‖光‖，何‖所‖不‖光‖昭‖。

translations.literal: Bright, bright is the light of sun and moon; what place do they not illumine?
translations.idiomatic: Bright, bright shines the light of sun and moon; what place lies beyond their reach?

sentences.zh: 二儀合聖化，貴者獨人不。

translations.literal: Heaven and Earth join in sage transformation; among the noble, none but man.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and Earth unite in sage transformation; among all that is noble, none surpasses man.

translations.literal: Within the myriad states and all the land, none is not the king's subject.
translations.idiomatic: Across the myriad states and all the realm, every man is the king's subject.

translations.literal: Benevolence and righteousness are one's fame; rites and music are one's glory.
translations.idiomatic: Benevolence and righteousness win renown; rites and music bring glory.

translations.literal: I sing to declare my intent: bright, bright is the light of sun and moon.
translations.idiomatic: I sing to declare my intent: bright, bright is the light of sun and moon.

translations.literal: Section Three
translations.idiomatic: Section Three

sentences.zh: 四‖時‖㪅‖逝‖去‖，晝‖夜‖以‖成‖歲‖。

translations.literal: The four seasons alternate and pass away; day and night together make the year.
translations.idiomatic: The four seasons turn and pass; day and night together weave the year.

translations.literal: The Great Man acts before Heaven, and Heaven does not oppose him.
translations.idiomatic: The sage acts before Heaven, and Heaven does not oppose him.

translations.literal: He does not grieve that years pass; he grieves that the age is not well governed.
translations.idiomatic: He does not mourn the passing years; he mourns that the age is not well governed.

translations.literal: Life and death have their allotted span; to brood over them is folly.
translations.idiomatic: Life and death are fated; to fret over them is folly.

translations.literal: I sing to declare my intent: the four seasons alternate and pass away.
translations.idiomatic: I sing to declare my intent: the four seasons turn and pass away.

translations.literal: Section Four
translations.idiomatic: Section Four

sentences.zh: 戚‖戚‖欲‖何‖念‖，歡‖笑‖意‖所‖之‖。

translations.literal: Sorrowful—what is there to brood on? Laughter and joy are where the heart would go.
translations.idiomatic: Why brood in sorrow? Laughter and joy are where the heart belongs.

translations.literal: The prime of strength and wisdom will never return.
translations.idiomatic: Youth's strength and wisdom will never come again.

translations.literal: Cherish the hour and press forward—whom will you benefit?
translations.idiomatic: Cherish the hour and press on—who will you benefit if you do not?

translations.literal: Drifting idly in dissipation—what difference does it make?
translations.idiomatic: To drift idly in dissipation—what is the difference?

translations.literal: I sing to declare my intent: sorrowful—what is there to brood on?
translations.idiomatic: I sing to declare my intent: sorrowful—what is there to brood on?

translations.literal: Section Five
translations.idiomatic: Section Five

translations.literal: "Ascending to Pay Court" / "Dongtao Ballad" — old lyrics
translations.idiomatic: "Ascending to Pay Court" (tune: "Dongtao Ballad") — traditional lyrics

translations.literal: Section Five
translations.idiomatic: Section Five

sentences.zh: 吾欲上謁從高山，山頭危嶮大難。

translations.literal: I wish to ascend and pay court from a high mountain; the summit is perilous and steep—great hardship.
translations.idiomatic: I wish to climb the high mountain and pay court above; the summit is perilous—no easy road.

sentences.zh: 遙望五嶽端，黃金為闕班璘。

translations.literal: Gazing from afar at the peaks of the Five Sacred Mountains, golden gates gleam in splendor.
translations.idiomatic: From afar I gaze at the Five Sacred Peaks, where golden gates gleam in splendor.

translations.literal: I see only spirit fungus; leaves fall in profusion.
translations.idiomatic: I see only spirit fungus; leaves drift down in showers.

translations.literal: Section One
translations.idiomatic: Section One

translations.literal: A hundred birds gather, coming like smoke.
translations.idiomatic: A hundred birds gather, arriving like drifting smoke.

translations.literal: Mountain beasts throng in profusion; qilin and pixie lead the way.
translations.idiomatic: Mountain beasts throng about; qilin and pixie lead the way.

sentences.zh: 鵾雞聲鳴，但見山獸，援戲相拘攀。

translations.literal: The kun-cock cries; I see only mountain beasts, playing together, holding and climbing on one another.
translations.idiomatic: The kun-cock cries; I see mountain beasts sporting together, clinging and climbing over one another.

translations.literal: Section Two
translations.idiomatic: Section Two

sentences.zh: 小復前行玉堂，未心懷流還。

translations.literal: Advancing a little further to the jade hall, my heart has not yet resolved to return.
translations.idiomatic: I press a little farther toward the jade hall; my heart has not yet turned homeward.

sentences.zh: 傳教出門來，門外人何求？

translations.literal: A messenger is sent out the gate: "What does the man outside seek?"
translations.idiomatic: A messenger is sent out the gate: "What does the man outside seek?"

sentences.zh: 所言欲從聖道，求一得命延。

translations.literal: He says he wishes to follow the sage Way and seek to obtain extended life.
translations.idiomatic: He says he wishes to follow the sage Way and win an extension of life.

translations.literal: Section Three
translations.idiomatic: Section Three

sentences.zh: 教敕凡吏受言，采取神藥若木端。

translations.literal: He commands the ordinary officials to receive his words and gather divine medicine from the tip of the Ruo tree.
translations.idiomatic: He commands the ordinary officials to heed his words and gather divine medicine from the tip of the Ruo tree.

sentences.zh: 白兔長跪擣藥蝦蟇丸，奉上陛下一玉柈，服此藥可得即仙。

translations.literal: A white hare kneels long, pounding medicine into toad pills; it presents to Your Majesty a jade platter—take this drug and at once become immortal.
translations.idiomatic: A white hare kneels and pounds the medicine into toad pills, then presents Your Majesty a jade platter: take this elixir and you will become immortal at once.

translations.literal: Section Four
translations.idiomatic: Section Four

translations.literal: Having taken your divine medicine, none fail to rejoice.
translations.idiomatic: Having taken the divine medicine, all rejoice.

sentences.zh: 陛下長生老壽，四面肅肅稽首，天神{扌雝}護左右，陛下長與天相保守。

translations.literal: May Your Majesty live long in eternal life; on every side all bow in reverence; heavenly spirits shield and protect at left and right—may Your Majesty long guard Heaven's mandate together with Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: May Your Majesty live forever; on every side all bow in reverence; heavenly spirits shield you on every hand—may Your Majesty long keep Heaven's mandate with Heaven.

translations.literal: Section Five
translations.idiomatic: Section Five

translations.literal: "Rushes Growing" / "Pond Journey Ballad" — lyrics by Emperor Wu
translations.idiomatic: "Rushes Growing" (tune: "Pond Journey Ballad") — text by Emperor Wu of Wei

translations.literal: Section Five
translations.idiomatic: Section Five

sentences.zh: 蒲‖生‖我‖池‖中‖，其葉何離離。

translations.literal: Rushes grow in my pond; how lush their leaves.
translations.idiomatic: Rushes grow in my pond; how lush their leaves spread.

sentences.zh: 傍能行儀儀，莫能縷自知。

translations.literal: Those beside can move with graceful bearing, yet none can thread through and know themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Outsiders may admire its grace, yet none can truly know it from within.

sentences.zh: 眾口鑠黃金，使君生別離。

translations.literal: Many mouths melt gold; they force my lord into parting.
translations.idiomatic: Many tongues can melt gold; slander has forced my lord and me apart.

translations.literal: Section One
translations.idiomatic: Section One

sentences.zh: 念‖君‖去‖我‖時‖，獨愁常苦悲。

translations.literal: When I think of the hour you left me, alone I grieve, ever bitter in sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: When I think of the hour you left me, I grieve alone, ever bitter in sorrow.

sentences.zh: 想見君顏色，感結傷心脾。

translations.literal: Longing to see your face, my heart knots in grief and wounds my spleen.
translations.idiomatic: Longing to see your face, grief knots my heart and wounds me to the core.

translations.literal: Now every night I grieve and cannot sleep.
translations.idiomatic: Now night after night I grieve and cannot sleep.

translations.literal: Section Two
translations.idiomatic: Section Two

sentences.zh: 莫‖用‖豪‖賢‖故‖，棄捐素所愛；

translations.literal: Do not for the sake of the powerful and worthy cast aside the one you have always loved;
translations.idiomatic: Do not for the sake of power and rank cast aside the one you have always loved;

sentences.zh: 莫用魚肉貴，棄捐蔥與薤；

translations.literal: do not because fish and meat are prized cast aside scallions and leeks;
translations.idiomatic: do not because fish and meat are prized cast aside scallions and leeks;

sentences.zh: 莫用麻枲賤，棄捐菅與蒯。

translations.literal: do not because hemp and ramie are cheap cast aside rush and sedge.
translations.idiomatic: do not because hemp and ramie are cheap cast aside rush and sedge.

translations.literal: Section Three
translations.idiomatic: Section Three

sentences.zh: 倍‖恩‖者‖苦‖栝‖，蹶船常苦沒。

translations.literal: Those who betray kindness suffer binding; an overturned boat constantly founders.
translations.idiomatic: Those who betray kindness suffer for it; a capsized boat is forever sinking.

sentences.zh: 教君安息定，慎莫致倉卒。

translations.literal: I teach you to rest in peace and be settled; take care not to act in haste.
translations.idiomatic: I urge you to rest in peace and be settled; take care not to act in haste.

sentences.zh: 念與君一共離別，亦當何時共坐復相對。

translations.literal: Thinking that you and I have parted together—when shall we sit together face to face again?
translations.idiomatic: Now that you and I are parted, when shall we sit together face to face again?

translations.literal: Section Four
translations.idiomatic: Section Four

sentences.zh: 出‖亦‖復‖苦‖愁‖，入亦復苦愁。

translations.literal: Going out, again bitter grief; coming in, again bitter grief.
translations.idiomatic: Going out brings bitter grief; coming in brings bitter grief again.

sentences.zh: 邊地多悲風，樹木何蕭蕭。

translations.literal: The borderlands have many mournful winds; how sighing the trees.
translations.idiomatic: The borderlands are full of mournful winds; how sighing the trees.

sentences.zh: 今日樂相樂，延年壽千秋。

translations.literal: Today let us rejoice together in joy; may life be extended a thousand autumns.
translations.idiomatic: Let us rejoice together while we may; may our lives extend a thousand years.

translations.literal: Section Five
translations.idiomatic: Section Five

translations.literal: "Far, Far" / "Bitter Cold Journey" — lyrics by Emperor Ming
translations.idiomatic: "Far, Far" (tune: "Bitter Cold Journey") — text by Emperor Ming of Wei

translations.literal: Section Five
translations.idiomatic: Section Five

sentences.zh: 悠‖悠‖發‖洛‖都‖，茾‖我‖征‖東‖行‖。

translations.literal: Far, far I depart from Luoyang; on my eastward campaign I go.
translations.idiomatic: Far, far I leave Luoyang behind; eastward on campaign I go.

sentences.zh: 征行彌二旬，屯吹隴陂城。

translations.literal: The campaign march has lasted twenty days; we encamp at Longpo Fort.
translations.idiomatic: The campaign march has lasted twenty days; we encamp at Longpo Fort.

translations.literal: Section One
translations.idiomatic: Section One

sentences.zh: 顧觀故‖壘‖處‖，皇‖祖‖之‖所‖營‖。

translations.literal: I look back at the old fortifications—the camp my imperial ancestor built.
translations.idiomatic: I look back at the old fortifications—the camp my imperial ancestor built.

sentences.zh: 屋室若平昔，棟宇無邪傾。

translations.literal: The dwellings are as in former days; beams and rafters show no crooked lean.
translations.idiomatic: The dwellings stand as in former days; beams and rafters show no crooked lean.

translations.literal: Section Two
translations.idiomatic: Section Two

sentences.zh: 奈何我‖皇‖祖‖，潛‖德‖隱‖聖‖形‖。

translations.literal: Alas for my imperial ancestor—hidden virtue, concealed sage's form.
translations.idiomatic: Alas for my imperial ancestor—virtue hidden, his sage's form withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 雖沒而不朽，書貴垂休名。

translations.literal: Though gone, he is not decayed; in writing his worth is honored and his fine name handed down.
translations.idiomatic: Though gone, he is not forgotten; in writing his worth is honored and his fine name endures.

translations.literal: Section Three
translations.idiomatic: Section Three

sentences.zh: 光光我‖皇‖祖‖，軒‖燿‖同‖其‖榮‖。

translations.literal: Bright, bright is my imperial ancestor; with Xuanyuan and Yaoh he shares their glory.
translations.idiomatic: Bright, bright shines my imperial ancestor; with Xuanyuan and Yaoh he shares their glory.

sentences.zh: 遺化布四海，八表以肅清。

translations.literal: His legacy spreads over the four seas; the eight directions are thereby made reverent and clear.
translations.idiomatic: His legacy spreads across the four seas; the eight directions stand reverent and clear.

translations.literal: Section Four
translations.idiomatic: Section Four

sentences.zh: 雖有吳‖蜀‖寇‖，春‖秋‖足‖燿‖兵。

translations.literal: Though there are Wu and Shu rebels, in spring and autumn our troops suffice to display martial glory.
translations.idiomatic: Though Wu and Shu still rebel, spring and autumn find our armies sufficient to display martial glory.

sentences.zh: 徒悲我皇祖，不永享百齡。

translations.literal: In vain I grieve for my imperial ancestor, who did not long enjoy a hundred years.
translations.idiomatic: In vain I grieve for my imperial ancestor, who did not live out a full hundred years.

sentences.zh: 賦詩以寫懷，伏軾淚沾纓。

translations.literal: I compose this poem to set forth my feelings; leaning on the chariot rail, tears soak my cap-strings.
