translations.idiomatic: In office in his district he never traded in favors.

translations.literal: He purified his person and toughened his body—early and late laboring diligently.
translations.idiomatic: He kept his body pure and labored early and late without rest.

translations.literal: His governance earned a name for ability—near and far all heard of it.
translations.idiomatic: His able rule made a name heard far and near.

translations.literal: Section Seven
translations.idiomatic: Seventh section

translations.literal: Heaven's years were not granted—early he sank into dusk.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven did not grant him long years—he died while still young.

translations.literal: For the magistrate they built a shrine—west of Anyang pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: They built him a shrine west of Anyang pavilion.

translations.literal: They wished later generations never to cease proclaiming his fame.
translations.idiomatic: They meant that later ages would never stop praising his name.

translations.literal: Section Eight
translations.idiomatic: Eighth section

sentences.zh: 《白頭吟》 與《櫂歌》同調 古詞

translations.literal: White-Haired Song—same tune as Oar Song—ancient lyrics
translations.idiomatic: White-Haired Song (same melody as Oar Song)—ancient text

translations.literal: Section Five
translations.idiomatic: Fifth section

sentences.zh: 晴如山上雲，皎若雲間月。

translations.literal: Clear as clouds on the mountain; bright as the moon between clouds.
translations.idiomatic: Clear as mountain clouds, bright as moonlight between the clouds.

sentences.zh: 聞君有兩意，故來相決絕。

translations.literal: I hear you harbor two intents—therefore I come to break off completely.
translations.idiomatic: I hear your heart is divided in two—so I have come to part for good.

translations.literal: Section One
translations.idiomatic: First section

sentences.zh: 平生共城中，何嘗斗酒會。

translations.literal: All our lives we shared the same town—when did we ever meet for a cup of wine?
translations.idiomatic: We lived together in the same city all our lives—yet we never once shared a cup of wine.

sentences.zh: 今日斗酒會，明旦溝水頭。

translations.literal: Today we meet for a cup of wine; tomorrow at the ditch's head.
translations.idiomatic: Today we share a cup of wine; tomorrow we stand at the ditch's edge.

sentences.zh: 蹀踥御溝上，溝水東西流。

translations.literal: Treading the imperial ditch above—the ditch waters flow east and west.
translations.idiomatic: Pacing the royal moat above—the waters run east and west.

translations.literal: Section Two
translations.idiomatic: Second section

sentences.zh: 郭東亦有樵，郭西亦有樵。

translations.literal: East of the outer wall there are woodcutters too; west of the outer wall there are woodcutters too.
translations.idiomatic: East of the suburb there is a woodcutter; west of the suburb there is a woodcutter too.

sentences.zh: 兩樵相推與，無親為誰驕？

translations.literal: Two woodcutters push and give to each other—with no kin, for whom do they show pride?
translations.idiomatic: Two woodcutters shove the load between them—with no family tie, who are they strutting for?

translations.literal: Section Three
translations.idiomatic: Third section

sentences.zh: 淒淒重淒淒，嫁娶亦不啼；

translations.literal: Desolate, again desolate—at marrying I do not weep;
translations.idiomatic: Grieving, ever grieving—I did not weep at my wedding;

sentences.zh: 願得一心人，白頭不相離。

translations.literal: I wish to gain a single-hearted man—to white-haired age never part.
translations.idiomatic: I only wanted one man whole in heart—to grow old together, never parted.

translations.literal: Section Four
translations.idiomatic: Fourth section

sentences.zh: 竹竿何嫋嫋，魚尾何離簁，男兒欲相知，何用錢刀為？

translations.literal: How gracefully sway the bamboo poles; how finely fringed the fish tails—if a man wishes to know another, what need is there for money and blades?
translations.idiomatic: The bamboo rod sways gently; the fish tail fans wide—if men would know each other, what need of gold or knives?

translations.literal: {齒立} like a horse chewing beanstalks; on the river the lofty gentleman disports.
translations.idiomatic: Halting like a horse chewing beanstalks, the noble gentleman sports by the stream.

sentences.zh: 今日相對樂，延年萬歲期。

translations.literal: Today we rejoice together in joy—a term of ten thousand years of extended life.
translations.idiomatic: Let us delight in each other today—may our joy last ten thousand years.

translations.literal: Section Five.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth section.

sentences.zh: 一本云：詞曰上有「紫羅咄咄奈何」。〉

translations.literal: One edition says: above the lyrics it reads 'Purple gauze—alas, what can be done.'
translations.idiomatic: One version notes that above the lyrics stands: 'Purple silk—ah, what can one do?'

translations.literal: Chu-mode plaintive poems
translations.idiomatic: Plaintive poems in Chu mode

translations.literal: Bright Moon—lyrics by the Prince of Dong'e
translations.idiomatic: Bright Moon—words by the Prince of Dong'e

translations.literal: Section Seven
translations.idiomatic: Seventh section

sentences.zh: 明月照高樓，流光正裴回。

translations.literal: Bright moon shines on the high tower; flowing light just now eddies and swirls.
translations.idiomatic: The bright moon lights the lofty tower; its radiance swirls and lingers.

sentences.zh: 上有愁思婦，悲歎有餘哀。

translations.literal: Above is a woman brooding in grief—mournful sighs with surplus sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: Above lives a woman lost in sorrow—her lament holds more grief than words can tell.

translations.literal: Section One
translations.idiomatic: First section

translations.literal: I ask who the sigher is.
translations.idiomatic: I ask: who is the one sighing?

translations.literal: She says herself: a traveler's wife.
translations.idiomatic: She answers: the wife of a man far from home.

sentences.zh: 夫行踰十載，賤妾常獨棲。

translations.literal: The husband's journey exceeds ten years; the lowly wife often dwells alone.
translations.idiomatic: Her husband has been gone more than ten years; she lives alone in her lowly room.

translations.literal: Section Two
translations.idiomatic: Second section

sentences.zh: 念君過於渴，思君劇於飢。

translations.literal: Thinking of you exceeds thirst; longing for you is sharper than hunger.
translations.idiomatic: Missing you is worse than thirst; longing for you cuts deeper than hunger.

sentences.zh: 君為高山栢，妾為濁水泥。

translations.literal: You are the cypress on the high mountain; I am the muddy water and dust.
translations.idiomatic: You are the cypress on the high hill; I am the muddy water and dust below.

translations.literal: Section Three
translations.idiomatic: Third section

sentences.zh: 北風行蕭蕭，烈烈入吾耳。

translations.literal: North wind goes sighing, sighing; fierce and sharp it enters my ears.
translations.idiomatic: The north wind sighs and sighs; its sharp breath pierces my ears.

sentences.zh: 心中念故人，淚墮不能止。

translations.literal: In my heart I think of the old friend; tears fall and cannot stop.
translations.idiomatic: My heart turns to my distant love; tears fall and will not cease.

translations.literal: Section Four
translations.idiomatic: Fourth section

sentences.zh: 沈浮各異路，會合當何諧？

translations.literal: Sinking and floating—each on a different road; when we meet, how can it harmonize?
translations.idiomatic: We drift on different currents—when we meet again, how can we be as one?

sentences.zh: 願作東北風，吹我入君懷。

translations.literal: I wish to become the northeast wind—blowing me into your bosom.
translations.idiomatic: I would be the northeast wind and blow myself into your arms.

translations.literal: Section Five
translations.idiomatic: Fifth section

sentences.zh: 君懷常不開，賤妾當何依。

translations.literal: Your bosom is constantly unopened—what should the lowly wife rely on?
translations.idiomatic: Your heart stays ever closed—what is left for me to cling to?

sentences.zh: 恩情中道絕，流止任東西。

translations.literal: Affection and grace cut off mid-road—drifting and stopping, east or west as it may.
translations.idiomatic: Love ended halfway—let the stream carry me east or west as it will.

translations.literal: Section Six
translations.idiomatic: Sixth section

sentences.zh: 我欲竟此曲，此曲悲且長。

translations.literal: I wish to finish this song—this song is mournful and long.
translations.idiomatic: I would sing this song to its end—this song is long and full of grief.

sentences.zh: 今日樂相樂，別後莫相忘！

translations.literal: Today let us rejoice together in joy—after parting do not forget each other!
translations.idiomatic: Let us rejoice together today—after we part, do not forget me!

translations.literal: Section Seven
translations.idiomatic: Seventh section

translations.idiomatic: Song Shu, Treatise 21—Textual Notes

translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen's 'Climbing the Mountain to Gaze Afar': the luxuriant growth of the grasses.

translations.idiomatic: ○ 'Of' (zhi) in the Wei Emperor Wen Collection reads 'lingzhi' (fungus).

sentences.zh: 武帝《蒿里行》，生民百遺一念之絕人腸。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu's Song Within the Artemisia Lane—the hundred of the living people, one thought cuts off human intestines.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu's 'Artemisia Lane': of the common people, a hundred remain—and one thought severs the heart.

translations.literal: ○ Jue—in the Collected Works of Emperor Wu of Wei reads 'break.'
translations.idiomatic: ○ 'Cut off' (jue) in the Wei Emperor Wu Collection reads 'break' (duan).

sentences.zh: 武帝《陌上桑》登彼九疑歷王門。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu's Mulberry Path—ascending those Nine Mysterious Peaks, passing the king's gate.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu's 'Mulberry Path': climbing the Nine Mysterious peaks, passing the king's gate.

translations.literal: ○ King's gate—in the Collected Works of Emperor Wu of Wei reads 'Jade Gate.'
translations.idiomatic: ○ 'King's gate' in the Wei Emperor Wu Collection reads 'Jade Gate.'

sentences.zh: 又絕人事游渾元若疾風游歘飄飄。

translations.literal: Also cutting off human affairs, roaming the primordial chaos like a swift wind roaming—suddenly, fluttering.
translations.idiomatic: Also: cutting off worldly ties, roaming primordial chaos like a gale—suddenly soaring, fluttering.

translations.literal: ○ Fluttering—in the Collected Works of Emperor Wu of Wei reads 'soaring and wheeling.'
translations.idiomatic: ○ 'Fluttering' in the Wei Emperor Wu Collection reads 'soaring and wheeling.'

translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen's 'Yan Song': 'dwelling' and 'roaming'—thought fills the bowels.

translations.literal: Section Four
translations.idiomatic: Fourth section

sentences.zh: 展詩清歌聊自寬，樂往哀來摧心肝。

translations.literal: I unfold a poem and sing a clear song to relieve myself somewhat; joy passes, sorrow comes—it crushes heart and liver.
translations.idiomatic: I unfold a poem and sing softly to ease my heart; joy fades and grief returns to crush my breast.

sentences.zh: 悲風清厲秋氣寒，羅幃徐動經秦軒。

translations.literal: Sad wind clear and sharp, autumn air cold; silk curtains slowly move, passing the Qin-style gallery.
translations.idiomatic: The bleak wind cuts cold through autumn; silk curtains stir slowly along the Qin-style gallery.

translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu's 'Short Song': 'Clear and bright as the bright moon—when can I grasp it?'

translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu's 'Autumn Hu Song': 'In rhyme and meaning the middle section describes distress.'

translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu's 'Bitter Cold Journey': 'North I climb Mount Taihang—how steep and towering the way!'

translations.idiomatic: Comment by your subject Chengcang

sentences.zh: 按：據下「五觧」之例，「巍巍」兩字皆當有疊聲。

translations.literal: Comment: according to the example of 'Section Five' below, both characters of 'towering' should carry reduplication.
translations.idiomatic: Note: by the pattern of 'Section Five' below, both characters of 'wei-wei' should show reduplication.

sentences.zh: 武帝《塘上行》：「傍能行儀儀。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu's Pond-Top Journey: 'At the side one can perform yi-yi.'
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu's 'Pond-Top Journey': 'By nature one can act with proper bearing.'

translations.literal: ○ 'Yi-yi'—one edition reads 'benevolent bearing.'
translations.idiomatic: ○ 'Yi-yi'—one edition reads 'benevolent bearing' (ren-yi).

sentences.zh: 文帝《善哉行》：「有得者能卒。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen's How Good: 'Those who gain it can finish.'
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen's 'How Good': 'Those who attain it can see it through.'

translations.literal: ○ Gain—in the Collected Works of Emperor Wen of Wei reads 'virtue.'
translations.idiomatic: ○ 'Gain' (de) in the Wei Emperor Wen Collection reads 'virtue' (de).

sentences.zh: 明帝《善哉行》：「虎臣列將，怫鬱免怒。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming's How Good: 'Tiger ministers and ranked generals—sullen anger dispelled, rage removed.'
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming's 'How Good': 'Tiger-like ministers and ranked generals—sullen wrath eased, anger cleared.'

translations.literal: ○ 'Removed'—one edition reads 'filled.'
translations.idiomatic: ○ 'Removed' (mian)—one edition reads 'filled' (chong).

sentences.zh: 古《西門行》：「何能坐愁，怫鬱當復來茲。

translations.literal: Ancient West Gate Song: 'How can one sit in grief—sullen and depressed, when will it come again here?'
translations.idiomatic: Ancient 'West Gate Song': 'How can I sit in brooding—when will this sullen gloom return?'

translations.literal: ○ One edition after 'again' has the character 'wait.'
translations.idiomatic: ○ One version adds 'wait' (dai) after 'again' (fu).

sentences.zh: 文帝《煌煌京洛行》：「淮陰五行，鳥得弓藏。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen's Splendid Capital Luoyang Journey: 'Huaiyin's five punishments—the bird gets the bow stored.'
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen's 'Splendid Luoyang Journey': 'Huaiyin's five punishments—when the bird is gone, the bow is stored.'

translations.literal: ○ In the Collected Works of Emperor Wen of Wei 'punishments' reads 'execution,' 'gets' reads 'exhausted.'
translations.idiomatic: ○ In the Wei Emperor Wen Collection 'xing' reads 'xing' (execution) and 'de' reads 'jin' (exhausted).

sentences.zh: 武帝《步出夏門行》：「驥老伏歷，志在千里。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu's Walking Out the Xia Gate: 'An old steed lies in the stable, yet its will is for a thousand li.'
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu's 'Walking Out the Xia Gate': 'An old steed lies in the stable, yet its will is for a thousand li.'

sentences.zh: 」○《魏武帝集》「驥老」作「老驥」，「歷」作「櫪」。

translations.literal: ○ In the Collected Works of Emperor Wu of Wei 'old steed' reads 'old steed,' 'stable' reads 'manger.'
translations.idiomatic: ○ In the Wei Emperor Wu Collection 'ji lao' reads 'lao ji' and 'li' reads 'li' (manger).

translations.literal: Also: 'The blessing of nurturing ease can obtain everlasting years.'
translations.idiomatic: Also: 'The blessing of nurturing ease can win long life.'

translations.literal: ' ○ Yi—in the Collected Works of Emperor Wu of Wei reads 'tranquil.'
translations.idiomatic: ○ 'Ease' (yi) in the Wei Emperor Wu Collection reads 'tranquil' (tian).

sentences.zh: 古《豔歌何嘗行》：「上慙滄浪之夫，下顧黃口小兒。

translations.literal: Ancient Splendid Song Have I Ever: 'Above I shame the man of the Canglang; below I look to the yellow-mouthed little children.'
translations.idiomatic: Ancient 'Splendid Song: Have I Ever': 'Above, I am shamed before the Canglang fisherman; below, I must care for my young at the breast.'

translations.literal: Your subject Chengcang
translations.idiomatic: Comment by your subject Chengcang

sentences.zh: 按：前《東門行》云「上用倉浪天」，故下為「黃口小兒」，此「夫」字亦當作「天」，滄浪言天之色如水也。

translations.literal: Comment: the earlier East Gate Song says 'above using the azure Heaven,' therefore below it is 'yellow-mouthed children'; this character 'man' also should read 'Heaven'—Canglang speaks of Heaven's color like water.
translations.idiomatic: Note: the earlier 'East Gate Song' has 'azure Heaven' above, so 'yellow-mouthed children' below; the word 'man' (fu) here should also be 'Heaven' (tian)—Canglang describes the sky's color as water.

sentences.zh: 欽定四庫全書薈要訂正

translations.literal: Imperial Siku Quanshu Essentials, Emendations
translations.idiomatic: Emendations to the Imperial Siku Quanshu Essentials edition

translations.literal: Respectfully
translations.idiomatic: Respectfully submitted

sentences.zh: 案卷二十第一頁後六行：「靈祚景祥」諸本「祚」訛「祁」，據郭茂倩《樂府》改。

translations.literal: Case: on the first page after line six of Treatise 20: 'The numinous mandate, auspicious omens'—in various editions 'mandate' (zuo) is wrongly 'Qi'; corrected following Guo Maoqian's Music Bureau collection.
translations.idiomatic: Note: Treatise 20, page 1, after line 6: 'Numinous mandate, propitious signs'—editions wrongly read 'Qi' for 'zuo'; corrected per Guo Maoqian's Music Bureau.

sentences.zh: 第十三頁前三行：「神考降饗」，按《晉書》「神」字作「祖」字。

translations.literal: Page 13, first three lines: 'The divine forefather descends to feast'—checking the Book of Jin, the character 'divine' reads 'ancestral.'
translations.idiomatic: Page 13, lines 1–3: 'The divine forefather descends to feast'—in the Book of Jin the word 'divine' is 'ancestral.'

sentences.zh: 第十四頁後二行：「纂宣之緒」，《刊本》「緒」訛「諸」，據《監本》改。

translations.literal: Page 14, last two lines: 'Continuing and proclaiming the thread'—in the Block edition 'thread' (xu) is wrongly 'various' (zhu); corrected following the Supervisory edition.
translations.idiomatic: Page 14, last 2 lines: 'Continuing the proclaimed line'—Block edition wrongly has 'zhu' for 'xu'; corrected per the Supervisory edition.

sentences.zh: 第二十八頁後八行：「我皇隆之」，諸本「隆」訛「降」，據郭茂倩《樂府》改。

translations.literal: Page 28, last eight lines: 'Our emperor exalts it'—in various editions 'exalt' (long) is wrongly 'descend' (jiang); corrected following Guo Maoqian's Music Bureau collection.
translations.idiomatic: Page 28, last 8 lines: 'Our emperor uplifts it'—editions wrongly read 'jiang' for 'long'; corrected per Guo Maoqian's Music Bureau.

sentences.zh: 第三十三頁後七行：「繼明紹世」，諸本「紹」訛「昭」，據郭茂倩《樂府》改。

translations.literal: Page 33, last seven lines: 'Continuing brightness, handing down the age'—in various editions 'hand down' (shao) is wrongly 'bright' (zhao); corrected following Guo Maoqian's Music Bureau collection.
translations.idiomatic: Page 33, last 7 lines: 'Continuing brightness, inheriting the age'—editions wrongly read 'zhao' for 'shao'; corrected per Guo Maoqian's Music Bureau.

sentences.zh: 第三十七頁前三行：「神武鷹揚」，諸本「鷹」訛「膺」，今改。

translations.literal: Page 37, first three lines: 'Divinely martial, eagle-soaring'—in various editions 'eagle' (ying) is wrongly 'breast' (ying); now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: Page 37, lines 1–3: 'Divinely martial, soaring like an eagle'—editions wrongly read 'ying' (breast) for 'ying' (eagle); emended.

sentences.zh: 第三十七頁後一行：「仰化青雲」，諸本「青」訛「清」，今改。

translations.literal: Page 37, last line: 'Looking up to transform the azure clouds'—in various editions 'azure' (qing) is wrongly 'clear' (qing); now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: Page 37, last line: 'Looking up to transform the blue clouds'—editions wrongly read 'clear' for 'azure'; emended.

sentences.zh: 第四十三頁後四行：「犠剛既陳」，諸本「犠」訛「儀」，據郭茂倩《樂府》改。

translations.literal: Page 43, last four lines: 'Sacrificial rams already set out'—in various editions 'sacrificial' (xi) is wrongly 'ceremony' (yi); corrected following Guo Maoqian's Music Bureau collection.
translations.idiomatic: Page 43, last 4 lines: 'Sacrificial rams already arrayed'—editions wrongly read 'yi' for 'xi'; corrected per Guo Maoqian's Music Bureau.

sentences.zh: 卷二十一第四頁前七行八行：「惟漢二十世」，刊本「十」下誤衍「二」字今刪。

translations.literal: Treatise 21, page 4, lines 7–8: 'Only Han's twentieth generation'—in the Block edition an extra 'two' is wrongly inserted after 'ten'; now deleted.
translations.idiomatic: Treatise 21, page 4, lines 7–8: 'Alas, Han's twentieth age'—Block edition wrongly adds 'two' after 'ten'; deleted.

sentences.zh: 第五頁後二行：「璧玉為軒堂」，《刊本》「軒」下衍「關」字，今刪。

translations.literal: Page 5, last two lines: 'Jade disks as hall and chamber'—in the Block edition an extra 'gate' is wrongly inserted after 'hall'; now deleted.
translations.idiomatic: Page 5, last 2 lines: 'Jade disks for hall and chamber'—Block edition wrongly adds 'gate' after 'hall'; deleted.

sentences.zh: 第六頁前七行：「白鹿脯」，《刊本》「脯」下衍「哺」字，據郭茂倩《樂府》刪。

translations.literal: Page 6, first seven lines: 'White deer jerky'—in the Block edition an extra 'suckle' is wrongly inserted after 'jerky'; deleted following Guo Maoqian's Music Bureau collection.
translations.idiomatic: Page 6, lines 1–7: 'White deer jerky'—Block edition wrongly adds 'bu' (suckle) after 'jerky'; deleted per Guo Maoqian's Music Bureau.

sentences.zh: 第七頁前五行：「新夷車駕」，新：《楚辭》本俱作「辛」。

translations.literal: Page 7, first five lines: 'New barbarian chariots and escort'—new: in all versions of the Songs of Chu it reads 'bitter' (xin).
translations.idiomatic: Page 7, lines 1–5: 'Fresh Yi chariots and escort'—'new' (xin): in all Chu Ci texts reads 'bitter' (xin).

sentences.zh: 第十一頁前八行：「我心何佛鬱」，佛：郭《樂府》本作「怫」。

translations.literal: Page 11, first eight lines: 'Why is my heart so vexed and heavy'—vexed: in Guo Maoqian's Music Bureau original reads 'sullen' (fu).
translations.idiomatic: Page 11, lines 1–8: 'Why is my heart so vexed'—'Buddha/vexed' (fo): Guo Maoqian's Music Bureau original has 'sullen' (fu).

sentences.zh: 第十三頁前一行：「采取神藥若木端」，諸本「木」訛「水」，今改。

translations.literal: Page 13, first line: 'Gathering divine medicine at the tip of the ruo tree'—in various editions 'tree' (mu) is wrongly 'water' (shui); now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: Page 13, line 1: 'Gathering divine elixir at the ruo tree's tip'—editions wrongly read 'water' for 'tree'; emended.

sentences.zh: 第十六頁後三行：「發枹若雷」，諸本「枹」訛「砲」，據郭茂倩《樂府》改。

translations.literal: Page 16, last three lines: 'Raising the drumstick like thunder'—in various editions 'drumstick' (bao) is wrongly 'cannon' (pao); corrected following Guo Maoqian's Music Bureau collection.
translations.idiomatic: Page 16, last 3 lines: 'Beating the drum like thunder'—editions wrongly read 'pao' (cannon) for 'bao' (drumstick); corrected per Guo Maoqian's Music Bureau.

sentences.zh: 第二十五頁後八行：「晴如山上雲」，郭茂倩《樂府》本「晴」作「皚」，「雲」作「雪」。

translations.literal: Page 25, last eight lines: 'Clear as clouds on the mountain'—in Guo Maoqian's Music Bureau original 'clear' (qing) reads 'white' (ai), 'cloud' (yun) reads 'snow' (xue).
translations.idiomatic: Page 25, last 8 lines: 'Clear as mountain clouds'—Guo Maoqian's Music Bureau has 'ai' (white) for 'qing' and 'snow' for 'cloud.'

sentences.zh: 第二十六頁前四行：「白頭不相離」下，《刊本》脫「四觧」二字；

translations.literal: Page 26, first four lines: below 'To white-haired age never part'—the Block edition omits the two characters 'Section Four';
translations.idiomatic: Page 26, lines 1–4: below 'never part in white-haired age'—Block edition drops the words 'Section Four';

sentences.zh: 六行：「延年萬歲期」下《刊本》脫「五觧」二字，今據前後例及本章題注增入。

translations.literal: Line six: below 'A term of ten thousand years of extended life' the Block edition omits the two characters 'Section Five'—now added following the examples before and after and this chapter's rubric notes.
translations.idiomatic: Line 6: below 'ten thousand years of extended life' the Block edition drops 'Section Five'—now restored following parallel sections and this chapter's headings.
